value.zh: 袷祭之禮，毀廟之主陳於太祖，未毀廟之主，皆升合食于太祖之室。
value.en: At the xia sacrifice, removed temple tablets are arrayed at the Grand Ancestor, while unremoved tablets are raised to share offerings in the Grand Ancestor's chamber.
value.literal: At the xia sacrifice, removed temple tablets are arrayed at the Grand Ancestor, while unremoved tablets are raised to share offerings in the Grand Ancestor's chamber.

value.zh: 太祖東向，昭南向，穆北向。
value.en: The Grand Ancestor faces east; zhao face south, and mu face north.
value.literal: The Grand Ancestor faces east; zhao face south, and mu face north.

value.zh: 太祖者，商之玄王、周之后稷是也。
value.en: The Grand Ancestors are exemplified by Xuan Wang of Shang and Hou Ji of Zhou.
value.literal: The Grand Ancestors are exemplified by Xuan Wang of Shang and Hou Ji of Zhou.

value.zh: 太祖之外，更無始祖。
value.en: Beyond the Grand Ancestor there is no additional founding ancestor.
value.literal: Beyond the Grand Ancestor there is no additional founding ancestor.

value.zh: 但商自玄王以後，十有四代，至湯而有天下。
value.en: From Shang's Xuan Wang to Tang's possession of the realm lay fourteen generations.
value.literal: From Shang's Xuan Wang to Tang's possession of the realm lay fourteen generations.

value.zh: 周自后稷已後，十有七代，至武王而有天下。
value.en: From Zhou's Hou Ji to King Wu's possession of the realm lay seventeen generations.
value.literal: From Zhou's Hou Ji to King Wu's possession of the realm lay seventeen generations.

value.zh: 其間代數既遠，遷廟親廟，皆出太祖之後，故得合食有序，尊卑不差。
value.en: Since those lines were remote, both removed temples and kin temples stood after the Grand Ancestor, so joint offerings had proper order and rank was not confused.
value.literal: Since those lines were remote, both removed temples and kin temples stood after the Grand Ancestor, so joint offerings had proper order and rank was not confused.

value.zh: 其後漢高祖受命，無始封祖，即以高皇帝為太祖。
value.en: When Han Gaozu received the mandate without a first-enfeoffed ancestor, he himself became Grand Ancestor.
value.literal: When Han Gaozu received the mandate without a first-enfeoffed ancestor, he himself became Grand Ancestor.

value.zh: 太上皇高帝之父，立廟享祀，不在昭穆合食之列，為尊于太祖故也。
value.en: Gaozu's father, the Grand Supreme Emperor, received a temple and sacrifices but was not included in the zhao-mu shared offerings, because he was honored above the Grand Ancestor.
value.literal: Gaozu's father, the Grand Supreme Emperor, received a temple and sacrifices but was not included in the zhao-mu shared offerings, because he was honored above the Grand Ancestor.

value.zh: 魏武創業，文帝受命，亦即以武帝為太祖。
value.en: Cao Cao founded Wei's enterprise, so when Emperor Wen received the mandate, Emperor Wu likewise became Grand Ancestor.
value.literal: Cao Cao founded Wei's enterprise, so when Emperor Wen received the mandate, Emperor Wu likewise became Grand Ancestor.

value.zh: 其高皇、太皇、外處君等並為屬尊，不在昭穆合食之列。
value.en: Gao Huang, Tai Huang, Waichu Jun, and the others were honored as kin and not included in the zhao-mu shared offerings.
value.literal: Gao Huang, Tai Huang, Waichu Jun, and the others were honored as kin and not included in the zhao-mu shared offerings.

value.zh: 晉宣創業，武帝受命，亦即以宣帝為太祖。
value.en: Sima Yi founded Jin's enterprise, so when Emperor Wu received the mandate, Emperor Xuan likewise became Grand Ancestor.
value.literal: Sima Yi founded Jin's enterprise, so when Emperor Wu received the mandate, Emperor Xuan likewise became Grand Ancestor.

value.zh: 其征西、豫章、潁川、京兆府君等並為屬尊，不在昭穆合食之列。
value.en: The Zhengxi, Yuzhang, Yingchuan, Jingzhao, and other lords were honored as kin and excluded from the zhao-mu shared offerings.
value.literal: The Zhengxi, Yuzhang, Yingchuan, Jingzhao, and other lords were honored as kin and excluded from the zhao-mu shared offerings.

value.zh: 歷茲已降，至於有隋，宗廟之制，斯禮不改。
value.en: From those dynasties through Sui, the ancestral-temple rule remained unchanged.
value.literal: From those dynasties through Sui, the ancestral-temple rule remained unchanged.

value.zh: 故宇文氏以文皇帝為太祖，隋室以武元皇帝為太祖。
value.en: Thus Northern Zhou treated Emperor Wen as Grand Ancestor, and Sui treated Emperor Wuyuan as Grand Ancestor.
value.literal: Thus Northern Zhou treated Emperor Wen as Grand Ancestor, and Sui treated Emperor Wuyuan as Grand Ancestor.

value.zh: 國家誕受在命，累葉重光。
value.en: Our dynasty received the mandate, and successive generations have renewed its brilliance.
value.literal: Our dynasty received the mandate, and successive generations have renewed its brilliance.

value.zh: 景皇帝始封唐公，實為太祖。
value.en: Emperor Jing, first enfeoffed as Duke of Tang, is truly the Grand Ancestor.
value.literal: Emperor Jing, first enfeoffed as Duke of Tang, is truly the Grand Ancestor.

value.zh: 中間代數既近，列在三昭三穆之內，故皇家太廟，唯有六室。
value.en: Because the line is still close and Emperor Jing falls within the three zhao and three mu, the Tang Grand Temple has only six chambers.
value.literal: Because the line is still close and Emperor Jing falls within the three zhao and three mu, the Tang Grand Temple has only six chambers.

value.zh: 其弘農府君、宣、光二帝，尊于太祖，親盡則遷，不在昭穆合食之數。
value.en: The Hongnong Lord, Emperor Xuan, and Emperor Guang stand in honor above the Grand Ancestor; once kinship is exhausted they are moved and are not part of the zhao-mu shared offerings.
value.literal: The Hongnong Lord, Emperor Xuan, and Emperor Guang stand in honor above the Grand Ancestor; once kinship is exhausted they are moved and are not part of the zhao-mu shared offerings.

value.zh: 今皇極再造，孝思匪寧。
value.en: Now the imperial order has been restored, and filial concern remains unsettled.
value.literal: Now the imperial order has been restored, and filial concern remains unsettled.

value.zh: 奉二月二十九日敕：「七室已下，依舊號尊崇。」
value.en: The edict of the twenty-ninth day of the second month said, "For the seven chambers and below, keep the old titles and honors."
value.literal: The edict of the twenty-ninth day of the second month said, "For the seven chambers and below, keep the old titles and honors."

value.zh: 又奉三月一日敕：「既立七廟，須尊崇始祖，速令詳之」者。
value.en: The edict of the first day of the third month added, "Since seven temples are being established, the founding ancestor must be honored. Examine this quickly."
value.literal: The edict of the first day of the third month added, "Since seven temples are being established, the founding ancestor must be honored. Examine this quickly."

value.zh: 伏尋禮經，始祖即是太祖，太祖之外，更無始祖。
value.en: Looking through the ritual classics, I find that the founding ancestor is the Grand Ancestor, and outside the Grand Ancestor there is no separate founder.
value.literal: Looking through the ritual classics, I find that the founding ancestor is the Grand Ancestor, and outside the Grand Ancestor there is no separate founder.

value.zh: 周朝太祖之外，以周文王為始祖，不合禮經。
value.en: For Zhou to set King Wen as a founding ancestor beyond the Grand Ancestor does not fit the ritual classics.
value.literal: For Zhou to set King Wen as a founding ancestor beyond the Grand Ancestor does not fit the ritual classics.

value.zh: 或有引《白虎通義》云「后稷為始祖、文王為太祖、武王為太宗」，及鄭玄注《詩·雍》序云「太祖謂文王」以為說者。
value.en: Some explain this by citing 《Baihu tongyi》, "Hou Ji was founding ancestor, King Wen Grand Ancestor, and King Wu Grand Zong," and Zheng Xuan's note to the 《Shi: Yong》 preface, "Grand Ancestor means King Wen."
value.literal: Some explain this by citing 《Baihu tongyi》, "Hou Ji was founding ancestor, King Wen Grand Ancestor, and King Wu Grand Zong," and Zheng Xuan's note to the 《Shi: Yong》 preface, "Grand Ancestor means King Wen."

value.zh: 其義不然。
value.en: That interpretation is wrong.
value.literal: That interpretation is wrong.

value.zh: 何者？
value.en: Why?
value.literal: Why?

value.zh: 彼以禮「王者祖有功，宗有德，周人祖文王而宗武王」，故謂文王為太祖耳，非袷祭群主合食之太祖。
value.en: They call King Wen Grand Ancestor because ritual says, "Rulers make ancestors of those with merit and zong of those with virtue; Zhou made King Wen ancestor and King Wu zong." But this is not the Grand Ancestor who receives all rulers in shared xia offerings.
value.literal: They call King Wen Grand Ancestor because ritual says, "Rulers make ancestors of those with merit and zong of those with virtue; Zhou made King Wen ancestor and King Wu zong." But this is not the Grand Ancestor who receives all rulers in shared xia offerings.

value.zh: 今之議者，或有欲立涼武昭王為始祖者，殊為不可。
value.en: Some now wish to make Liang Wuzhao Wang the founding ancestor, but this is especially wrong.
value.literal: Some now wish to make Liang Wuzhao Wang the founding ancestor, but this is especially wrong.

value.zh: 何者？
value.en: Why?
value.literal: Why?

value.zh: 昔在商、周，契、稷始封，湯、武之興，祚由契、稷，故以契、稷為太祖，即皇家之景帝是也。
value.en: In Shang and Zhou, Xie and Hou Ji were the first enfeoffed ancestors. Tang and Wu rose from their fortune, so Xie and Hou Ji became Grand Ancestors. For our imperial house, that role belongs to Emperor Jing.
value.literal: In Shang and Zhou, Xie and Hou Ji were the first enfeoffed ancestors. Tang and Wu rose from their fortune, so Xie and Hou Ji became Grand Ancestors. For our imperial house, that role belongs to Emperor Jing.

value.zh: 涼武昭王勳業未廣，後主失國，土宇不傳。
value.en: Liang Wuzhao Wang's merit was limited, his successor lost the state, and the territory did not continue.
value.literal: Liang Wuzhao Wang's merit was limited, his successor lost the state, and the territory did not continue.

value.zh: 景皇始封，實基明命。
value.en: Emperor Jing's first enfeoffment truly founded the Tang mandate.
value.literal: Emperor Jing's first enfeoffment truly founded the Tang mandate.

value.zh: 今乃舍封唐之盛烈，崇西涼之遠構，考之前古，實乖典禮。
value.en: To abandon the great enfeoffment in Tang and exalt distant Western Liang violates ancient ritual precedent.
value.literal: To abandon the great enfeoffment in Tang and exalt distant Western Liang violates ancient ritual precedent.

value.zh: 魏氏不以曹參為太祖，晉氏不以殷王仰為太祖，宋氏不以楚元王為太祖，齊、梁不以蕭何為太祖，陳、隋不以胡公、楊震為太祖，則皇家安可以涼武昭王為太祖乎？
value.en: Wei did not ancestralize Cao Shen, Jin did not ancestralize the King of Yin, Song did not ancestralize King Yuan of Chu, Qi and Liang did not ancestralize Xiao He, and Chen and Sui did not ancestralize Duke Hu or Yang Zhen. How could Tang make Liang Wuzhao Wang Grand Ancestor?
value.literal: Wei did not ancestralize Cao Shen, Jin did not ancestralize the King of Yin, Song did not ancestralize King Yuan of Chu, Qi and Liang did not ancestralize Xiao He, and Chen and Sui did not ancestralize Duke Hu or Yang Zhen. How could Tang make Liang Wuzhao Wang Grand Ancestor?

value.zh: 漢之東京，大議郊祀，多以周郊后稷，漢當郊堯。
value.en: In Eastern Han, a major debate over suburban sacrifice held that because Zhou offered to Hou Ji, Han should offer to Yao.
value.literal: In Eastern Han, a major debate over suburban sacrifice held that because Zhou offered to Hou Ji, Han should offer to Yao.

value.zh: 制上公卿議，議者多同，帝亦然之。
value.en: The court sent the issue to the ministers; most agreed, and the emperor was inclined to agree as well.
value.literal: The court sent the issue to the ministers; most agreed, and the emperor was inclined to agree as well.

value.zh: 杜林正議，獨以為「周室之興，祚由后稷。
value.en: Only Du Lin argued correctly: "The rise of Zhou came through Hou Ji.
value.literal: Only Du Lin argued correctly: "The rise of Zhou came through Hou Ji.

value.zh: 漢業特起，功不緣堯。
value.en: Han arose on its own; its merit did not derive from Yao.
value.literal: Han arose on its own; its merit did not derive from Yao.

value.zh: 祖宗故事，所宜因循。」
value.en: The old precedents for ancestors and zong should be followed."
value.literal: The old precedents for ancestors and zong should be followed."

value.zh: 竟從林議。
value.en: The court ultimately followed Du Lin.
value.literal: The court ultimately followed Du Lin.

value.zh: 又傳稱，「欲知天上，事問長人」，以其近之。
value.en: Another tradition says, "To know Heaven, ask the elders," because they stand closer to it.
value.literal: Another tradition says, "To know Heaven, ask the elders," because they stand closer to it.

value.zh: 武德、貞觀之時，主聖臣賢，其去涼武昭王蓋亦近於今矣。
value.en: The Wude and Zhenguan rulers were sagely and their ministers worthy, and they were closer to Liang Wuzhao Wang's time than we are.
value.literal: The Wude and Zhenguan rulers were sagely and their ministers worthy, and they were closer to Liang Wuzhao Wang's time than we are.

value.zh: 當時不立者，必不可立故也。
value.en: If they did not establish him then, he surely should not be established now.
value.literal: If they did not establish him then, he surely should not be established now.

value.zh: 今既年代浸遠，方復立之，是非三祖二宗之意。
value.en: To establish him only after so many years would violate the intent behind the three ancestors and two zong.
value.literal: To establish him only after so many years would violate the intent behind the three ancestors and two zong.

value.zh: 實恐景皇失職而震怒，武昭虛位而不答，非社稷之福也。
value.en: I fear Emperor Jing would be displaced and angered, while Wuzhao would hold an empty position and give no response; this would not benefit the state.
value.literal: I fear Emperor Jing would be displaced and angered, while Wuzhao would hold an empty position and give no response; this would not benefit the state.

value.zh: 宗廟事重，禘祫禮崇，先王以之觀德。
value.en: Temple affairs are weighty, and the di and xia rites are exalted; through them the former kings observed virtue.
value.literal: Temple affairs are weighty, and the di and xia rites are exalted; through them the former kings observed virtue.

value.zh: 或者不知其說，既灌而往，孔子不欲觀之。
value.en: Some fail to understand this. Confucius himself did not wish to watch after the libation had passed.
value.literal: Some fail to understand this. Confucius himself did not wish to watch after the libation had passed.

value.zh: 今朝命惟新，宜應慎禮，祭如神在，理不可誣。
value.en: Now that the dynasty's mandate has been renewed, ritual must be handled carefully. Sacrifice is performed as if the spirits were present; it cannot be falsified.
value.literal: Now that the dynasty's mandate has been renewed, ritual must be handled carefully. Sacrifice is performed as if the spirits were present; it cannot be falsified.

value.zh: 請准敕加太廟為七室，享宣皇帝以備七代，其始祖不合別有尊崇。
value.en: I request that the Grand Temple be expanded to seven chambers and Emperor Xuan be sacrificed to as the seventh generation; no separate honor should be given to another founding ancestor.
value.literal: I request that the Grand Temple be expanded to seven chambers and Emperor Xuan be sacrificed to as the seventh generation; no separate honor should be given to another founding ancestor.

value.zh: 褚遂良 韓瑗 來濟 上官儀
value.en: Chu Suiliang, Han Yuan, Lai Ji, and Shang Guanyi
value.literal: Chu Suiliang, Han Yuan, Lai Ji, Shang Guanyi

value.zh: 臣聞有國家者譬諸身，兩京等於心腹，四境方乎手足，他方絕域，若在身外。
value.en: I have heard that one who possesses a state may be compared to the body. The two capitals are like the heart and belly, the four borders like the hands and feet, and other regions and distant realms are as if outside the body.
value.literal: This subject has heard that one who has a state is compared to the body—the two capitals equal the heart and belly, the four borders are like the hands and feet, other regions and distant realms are as if outside the body.

value.zh: 臣近於坐下，伏奉口敕，布語臣下，雲自欲伐遼。
value.en: Recently below Your seat I received an oral edict, promulgated to your ministers below, saying that you yourself wish to attack Liao.
value.literal: This subject recently below Your seat, prostrate received oral edict, promulgated words to ministers below, saying you yourself wish to attack Liao.

value.zh: 臣數夜思量，不達其理。
value.en: For several nights I have pondered this and cannot understand its rationale.
value.literal: This subject for several nights pondered and could not reach its principle.

value.zh: 高麗王為陛下之所立，莫離支輒殺其主，陛下討逆收地，斯實乘機。
value.en: The King of Goryeo was established by Your Majesty. Yeon Gaesomun abruptly killed his lord. For Your Majesty to punish the rebel and recover the territory is truly to seize the opportune moment.
value.literal: The King of Goryeo was established by Your Majesty; Yeon Gaesomun abruptly killed his lord—Your Majesty punishing rebellion and recovering territory is truly seizing the opportunity.

value.zh: 關東賴陛下德澤，久無征戰，但命二、三勇將，發兵四、五萬，飛石輕梯，取如回掌。
value.en: Guandong relies on Your Majesty's virtue and grace and has long been free of warfare. You need only command two or three brave generals and send forth forty or fifty thousand troops. With flying stones and light ladders, taking it would be like turning the palm.
value.literal: Guandong relies on Your Majesty's virtue and favor, long without campaigns and battles—only command two or three brave generals, send forth forty or fifty thousand troops, flying stones and light ladders, taking it like turning the palm.

value.zh: 夫聖人有作，必履常規，貴能克平凶亂，駕馭才傑。
value.en: When a sage acts, he must follow constant norms, valuing the ability to overcome fierce disorder and to drive and control talented heroes.
value.literal: The sage when he acts must tread constant norms, valuing the ability to overcome and pacify fierce disorder and to drive and control talented heroes.

value.zh: 惟陛下弘兩儀之道，扇三五之風，提厲人物，皆思效命。
value.en: Your Majesty alone expands the Way of the Two Principles and fans the wind of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, lifting and sharpening men of talent, all of whom wish to offer their lives.
value.literal: Only Your Majesty expands the Way of the Two Principles, fans the wind of the Three and Five, lifts and sharpens men and things—all think to offer their lives.

value.zh: 昔侯君集、李靖，所謂庸夫，猶能掃萬里之高昌，平千載之突厥，皆是陛下發蹤指示，聲歸聖明。
value.en: Formerly Hou Junji and Li Jing, so-called mediocre men, still swept Gaochang ten thousand li away and pacified the Turks of a thousand years—all because Your Majesty set them on the track and gave directions, and the credit returned to your sagely brilliance.
value.literal: Formerly Hou Junji and Li Jing, so-called mediocre men, still could sweep ten-thousand-li Gaochang and pacify thousand-year Turks—all were Your Majesty issuing tracks and giving directions, reputation returning to sagely brilliance.

value.zh: 臣旁求史籍，訖乎近代，為人之主，無自伐遼，人臣往征，則有之矣。
value.en: I have searched the histories on every side down to recent times. As ruler of men, none has personally campaigned against Liao, though as ministers going on campaign there have been such cases.
value.literal: This subject searched history on every side down to recent times—as ruler of men, none personally campaigned against Liao; as ministers going on campaign, there have been such cases.

value.zh: 漢朝則荀彘、楊僕，魏代則毋丘儉、王頎；
value.en: In the Han dynasty there were Xun Yi and Yang Pu; in the Wei era there were Wuqiu Jian and Wang Qi;
value.literal: Han dynasty then Xun Yi and Yang Pu; Wei era then Wuqiu Jian and Wang Qi;

value.zh: 司馬懿猶為人臣，慕容真僭號之子，皆為其主長驅高麗，虜其人民，削平城壘。
value.en: Sima Yi was still a minister of men, and Murong Zhen was the son of a usurper—all of them for their lords drove deep into Goryeo, captured its people, and leveled walls and ramparts.
value.literal: Sima Yi was still a minister of men; Murong Zhen was a son who usurped a title—all for their lords drove far into Goryeo, captured its people, and leveled walls and ramparts.

value.zh: 陛下立功同於天地，美化包於古昔，自當超邁於百王，豈止俯同於六子？
value.en: Your Majesty's achievements equal Heaven and Earth, and your civilizing transformation embraces antiquity. You should naturally surpass the hundred kings—how could you merely bow to match the six sons?
value.literal: Your Majesty's establishment of achievement equals Heaven and Earth, civilizing transformation embraces antiquity—you should naturally surpass the hundred kings, how only bow to match the six sons?

value.zh: 陛下昔翦平寇逆，大有爪牙，年齒未衰，猶堪任用，匪唯陛下之所使，亦何行而不克。
value.en: Your Majesty formerly cut down bandit rebels and greatly possessed capable men. Your years are not yet declined and they are still fit for employment. Not only can Your Majesty employ them—what undertaking would they not succeed in?
value.literal: Your Majesty formerly cut down and pacified bandit rebels, greatly possessing claws and fangs; years not yet declined, still fit for employment—not only those Your Majesty can employ, what undertaking would not succeed?

value.zh: 方今太子新立，年實幼少，自余籓屏，陛下所知。
value.en: Just now the crown prince has been newly established and is truly young. As for the rest of the princely screen, Your Majesty knows them well.
value.literal: Just now the Crown Prince is newly established, years truly young and small; the rest of the screen of vassals Your Majesty knows.

value.zh: 今一旦棄金湯之全，渡遼海之外，臣忽三思，煩愁並集。
value.en: Now, in a single morning, to abandon the completeness of metal and boiling water and cross beyond the Liao Sea—when I think of it three times over, worry and sorrow gather together.
value.literal: Now in one morning abandoning the completeness of metal and boiling water, crossing beyond the Liao Sea—this subject suddenly thrice thinks, worry and sorrow together gather.

value.zh: 大魚依於巨海，神龍據於川泉，此謂人君不可輕而遠也。
value.en: Great fish rely on the vast sea, and the divine dragon occupies streams and springs. This means that the ruler of men cannot lightly go far from home.
value.literal: Great fish rely on the vast sea; divine dragon occupies streams and springs—this means the ruler of men cannot be lightly made distant.

value.zh: 且以長遼之左，或遇霖淫，水潦騰波，平地數尺。
value.en: Moreover, along the left bank of the long Liao, one may meet prolonged rain, when floods surge in waves and the level ground stands several feet deep.
value.literal: Moreover along the left of long Liao, one may meet prolonged rain; floods surge in waves, level ground several feet.

value.zh: 夫帶方、玄菟，海途深渺，非萬乘所宜行踐。
value.en: Daifang and Xuantu lie along a sea route deep and vast—not a path that the Son of Heaven should tread.
value.literal: Daifang and Xuantu—the sea route deep and vast, not what ten-thousand chariots should tread.

value.zh: 東京太原，謂之中地，東捴可以為聲勢，西指足以摧延陀，其於西京，逕路非遠，為其節度，以設軍謀，系莫離支頸，獻皇家之廟。
value.en: The Eastern Capital at Taiyuan is called the central land. A gathering to the east can serve as momentum, and a thrust to the west suffices to crush Xueyantuo. As for the Western Capital, the direct route is not far. Make dispositions from there, set military plans, tie Yeon Gaesomun by the neck, and present his head in the imperial clan temple.
value.literal: Eastern Capital Taiyuan is called the central land—eastward gathering can serve as sound and momentum, westward pointing suffices to crush Xueyantuo; as for Western Capital, the direct route is not far, make dispositions for it, set military plans, tie Yeon Gaesomun's neck, present to the imperial clan temple.

value.zh: 此實處安全之上計，社稷之根本，特乞天慈，一垂省察。
value.en: This is truly the best plan for dwelling in security and the root of the altars of state. I specially beg your heavenly kindness to examine it once.
value.literal: This is truly the upper plan for dwelling in security, the root of altars of soil and grain—I specially beg heavenly kindness, once to extend examination.

value.zh: 韓滉，字太沖，太子少師休之子也。
value.en: Han Huang, courtesy name Taichong, was the son of Xiu, who had served as Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.
value.literal: Han Huang, styled Taichong, was a son of Xiu, Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.

value.zh: 少貞介好學，以廕解褐左威衛騎曹參軍，出為同官主簿。
value.en: As a young man he was upright and studious; through hereditary privilege he began his career as cavalry adjutant in the Left Weiming Guard and was later posted as registrar at Tongguan.
value.literal: In youth he was upright and fond of learning; through yin privilege he entered service as Cavalry Army Adjutant of the Left Weiming Guard, and went out as registrar at Tongguan.

value.zh: 至德初，青齊節度鄧景山辟為判官，授監察御史、兼北海郡司馬，以道路阻絕，因避地山南。
value.en: Early in the Zhide era, Deng Jingshan, military governor of Qing and Qi, took him on as aide; he received appointment as investigative censor and concurrent militia marshal of Beihai commandery; when travel routes were cut off, he withdrew to the Shannan region.
value.literal: At the beginning of the Zhide era, Deng Jingshan, commissioner of Qing-Qi, recruited him as aide; he was appointed Investigative Censor and concurrently Militia Marshal of Beihai; because roads were blocked, he took refuge in Shannan.

value.zh: 采訪使李承昭奏充判官，授通州長史、彭王府諮議參軍。
value.en: The investigation commissioner Li Chengzhao memorialized that he serve as aide; he was granted the posts of tongzhou administrator and staff adviser in the Prince of Peng's establishment.
value.literal: Investigation Commissioner Li Chengzhao memorialized appointing him aide; he was appointed Administrator of Tongzhou and Staff Adviser of the Prince of Peng's household.

value.zh: 鄧景山移鎮淮南，又表為賓佐，未行，除殿中侍御史，追赴京師。
value.en: When Deng Jingshan moved his headquarters to Huainan, he again nominated Huang as a staff aide; before Huang could take up the post, he was appointed palace attendant censor and ordered to the capital.
value.literal: When Deng Jingshan transferred his command to Huainan, he again memorialized for him as staff aide; before he could go, he was appointed Palace Attendant Censor and summoned to the capital.

value.zh: 先是，滉兄法知制誥，草王玙拜官之詞，不加虛美，玙頗銜之。
value.en: Earlier, Huang's elder brother Fa had been responsible for drafting edicts; when he composed the text appointing Wang Yu, he had not padded it with empty praise, and Yu took strong offense.
value.literal: Earlier, Huang's elder brother Fa had charge of edict drafting; when drafting Wang Yu's appointment text, he did not add empty flattery, and Yu deeply resented it.

value.zh: 及其秉政，諸使奏滉兄弟者，必以冗官授之。
value.en: Once Yu was in power, whenever memorials came in concerning the Huang brothers, he always assigned them to nominal posts.
value.literal: When Yu held power, whenever envoys memorialized about the Huang brothers, he always gave them idle appointments.

value.zh: 玙免相，群議稱其屈，累遷至祠部、孝功、吏部三員外郎。
value.en: After Yu was removed from the chancellorship, opinion held that they had been treated unjustly; Huang rose in succession through external vacancies in the ministries of rites, filial achievement, and personnel.
value.literal: When Yu left the chancellorship, public comment held that they had been wronged; Huang was successively promoted to external vacancy in the Rites, Filial Achievement, and Personnel ministries.

value.zh: 臯生知音律，嘗觀彈琴，至《止息》，嘆曰：「妙哉！
value.en: Gao had an innate understanding of pitch and musical law. Once, watching someone play the zither, when the player reached "Stopping and Resting," he sighed, "Marvelous!
value.literal: Gao from birth understood pitch and law; once watching someone play the zither, when they reached "Stopping and Resting," he sighed: "Wonderful!

value.zh: 嵇生之為是曲也，其當晉、魏之際乎！
value.en: When Master Ji composed this piece, must it not have been at the turning point between Jin and Wei!
value.literal: When Master Ji composed this piece, must it not have been at the juncture of Jin and Wei!

value.zh: 其音主商，商為秋聲。
value.en: Its tone is dominated by the shang mode, and shang is the sound of autumn.
value.literal: Its tone is dominated by shang; shang is the sound of autumn.

value.zh: 秋也者，天將搖落肅殺，其歲之晏乎！
value.en: Autumn is when heaven shakes the leaves down in bleak severity—is it not the year's decline!
value.literal: Autumn—heaven about to shake down, wither, and kill in severity—is it not the year's decline!

value.zh: 又晉乘金運，商，金聲，此所以知魏之季而晉將代也。
value.en: Jin, moreover, rode the fortune of metal, and shang is the sound of metal—by this one knows that Wei was in its last days and Jin was about to replace it.
value.literal: Also Jin rode the fortune of metal; shang is the sound of metal—by this one knows the end of Wei and Jin about to replace it.

value.zh: 慢其商弦，與宮同音，是臣奪君之義也，所以知司馬氏之將篡也。
value.en: Loosen the shang strings until they match the palace tone, and that is the image of a subject seizing his lord—by this one knows the Sima clan was about to usurp the throne.
value.literal: If one loosens its shang strings to match palace in tone, that is the meaning of subject seizing lord—by this one knows the Sima clan was about to usurp.

value.zh: 司馬懿受魏明帝顧托後嗣，反有篡奪之心，自誅曹爽，逆節彌露。
value.en: Sima Yi had received Wei Emperor Ming's deathbed charge to protect the successor, yet harbored thoughts of usurpation; from the killing of Cao Shuang onward, his treasonous intent showed ever more plainly.
value.literal: Sima Yi received Wei Emperor Ming's deathbed charge for the successor, yet harbored usurpation in mind; from killing Cao Shuang, his rebellious intent showed ever more.

value.zh: 王陵都督揚州，謀立荊王彪；
value.en: Wang Ling, governor of Yang province, plotted to install Prince Jing Biao;
value.literal: Wang Ling as governor of Yang province plotted to install Prince Jing Biao;

value.zh: 毋丘儉、文欽、諸葛誕前後相繼為揚州都督，咸有匡復魏室之謀，皆為懿父子所殺。
value.en: Wuqiu Jian, Wen Qin, and Zhuge Dan served in succession as governors of Yang province, each with plans to restore the house of Wei, and each was killed by Yi and his sons.
value.literal: Wuqiu Jian, Wen Qin, and Zhuge Dan in succession governed Yang—each had plans to restore the Wei house—all were killed by Yi and his sons.

value.zh: 叔夜以揚州故廣陵之地，彼四人者，皆魏室文武大臣，咸敗散於廣陵，《散》言魏氏散亡，自廣陵始也。
value.en: Jiye took Yangzhou's old territory of Guangling—those four men were all great civil and military ministers of Wei, all defeated and scattered at Guangling; "Scatter" means the dispersal and ruin of Wei, beginning at Guangling.
value.literal: Jiye took Yangzhou's former Guangling territory—those four men were all Wei civil and military great ministers, all defeated and scattered at Guangling; "Scatter" speaks of Wei's dispersal and ruin, beginning from Guangling.

value.zh: 《止息》者，晉雖暴興，終止息於此也。
value.en: "Stopping and Resting" means that though Jin rose violently, it would in the end come to rest here.
value.literal: "Stopping and Resting"—though Jin rose violently, it would in the end stop and rest here.

value.zh: 其哀憤躁蹙，憯痛迫脅之旨，盡在於是矣。
value.en: Its grief, rage, agitation, compression, bitter pain, and sense of forced constraint—all of that intent is contained in this piece.
value.literal: Its grief, rage, agitation, compression, bitter pain, and forced constraint—all intent is in this.

value.zh: 永嘉之亂，其應乎！
value.en: The Yongjia disaster—is this its fulfillment!
value.literal: The Yongjia disorder—is this its response!

value.zh: 叔夜撰此，將貽後代之知音者，且避晉、魏之禍，所以托之神鬼也。」
value.en: Jiye composed this to bequeath it to later generations who would understand, and also to avoid the disasters of Jin and Wei—therefore he entrusted it to spirits and ghosts."
value.literal: Jiye composed this to bequeath to later generations who understand tone, and also to avoid Jin-Wei disaster—therefore he entrusted it to spirits and ghosts."

value.zh: 禮志上
value.en: Rites Treatise, Part One
value.literal: Treatises on Rites, Part One

value.zh: 〈（案：《禮志序》，原本闕佚。）〉
value.en: (Editor's note: The preface to the Treatise on Rites is no longer extant in the original.)
value.literal: (Note: The preface to the Treatise on Rites is missing from the original text.)

value.zh: 臣讀十四代史書，見二千年故事，觀諸家宗廟，都無始祖之稱，唯商、周二代，以稷、契為太祖。
value.en: I have read the histories of fourteen dynasties and reviewed two thousand years of precedent; in every dynasty's ancestral temples there is no title of founding ancestor—only in the Shang and Zhou were Ji and Qi taken as Taizu.
value.literal: I have read the histories of fourteen dynasties and reviewed two thousand years of precedent; in every dynasty's ancestral temples there is no title of founding ancestor—only in the Shang and Zhou were Ji and Qi taken as Taizu.

value.zh: 《禮記》曰：「天子七廟，三昭、三穆，與太祖之廟而七。」
value.en: The Record of Rites states: "The Son of Heaven has seven temples: three zhao, three mu, and the Taizu temple—seven in all."
value.literal: The 《Record of Rites》 says: "The Son of Heaven has seven temples: three zhao, three mu, and the Taizu temple—seven in all."

value.zh: 鄭玄註：「此周制也。
value.en: Zheng Xuan's annotation: "This is the Zhou system.
value.literal: Zheng Xuan's annotation: "This is the Zhou system.

value.zh: 七者，太祖後稷及文王、武王與四親廟。」
value.en: The seven are the Taizu Hou Ji, Kings Wen and Wu, and the four collateral-line temples."
value.literal: The seven are the Taizu Hou Ji, Kings Wen and Wu, and the four collateral-line temples."

value.zh: 又曰：「商人六廟，契及成湯與二昭、二穆也。
value.en: It further states: "The Shang had six temples: Qi and Cheng Tang, together with two zhao and two mu chambers.
value.literal: It further says: "The Shang had six temples: Qi and Cheng Tang, together with two zhao and two mu chambers.

value.zh: 夏後氏立五廟，不立太祖，惟禹與二昭、二穆而已。」
value.en: The Xia Hou clan established five temples and did not establish a Taizu—only Yu together with two zhao and two mu chambers."
value.literal: The Xia Hou clan established five temples and did not establish a Taizu—only Yu together with two zhao and two mu chambers."

value.zh: 據《王制》鄭玄所釋，即商、周以稷、契為太祖，夏後無太祖，亦無追謚之廟。
value.en: According to Zheng Xuan's explanation of the Royal Regulations, the Shang and Zhou took Ji and Qi as Taizu; the Xia Hou had no Taizu and also no posthumously enshrined temple.
value.literal: According to Zheng Xuan's explanation of the 《Royal Regulations》, the Shang and Zhou took Ji and Qi as Taizu; the Xia Hou had no Taizu and also no posthumously enshrined temple.

value.zh: 自商、周以來，時更十代，皆於親廟之中，以有功者為太祖，無追崇始祖之例。
value.en: Since the Shang and Zhou, ten dynasties have passed; all, within the collateral temples, took the meritorious figure as Taizu—there is no precedent for posthumously honoring a founding ancestor.
value.literal: Since the Shang and Zhou, ten dynasties have passed; all, within the collateral temples, took the meritorious figure as Taizu—there is no precedent for posthumously honoring a founding ancestor.

value.zh: 具引今古，即恐詞繁，事要證明，須陳梗概。
value.en: To cite ancient and modern cases in full would make the language prolix; since the matter requires proof, I must set forth the outline.
value.literal: To cite ancient and modern cases in full would make the language prolix; since the matter requires proof, I must set forth the outline.

value.zh: 漢以高祖父太上皇執嘉無社稷功，不立廟號，高帝自為高祖。
value.en: The Han, because the great-grandfather the Supreme Emperor Zhijia had no merit for the state, did not establish a temple title; the High Emperor himself served as Gaozu.
value.literal: The Han, because the great-grandfather the Supreme Emperor Zhijia had no merit for the altars of soil and grain, did not establish a temple title; the High Emperor himself served as Gaozu.

value.zh: 魏以曹公相漢，垂三十年，始封於魏，故為太祖。
value.en: The Wei, because Duke Cao served as chancellor of Han for nearly thirty years and was first enfeoffed in Wei, made him Taizu.
value.literal: The Wei, because Duke Cao served as chancellor of Han for nearly thirty years and was first enfeoffed in Wei, made him Taizu.

value.zh: 晉以宣王輔魏有功，立為高祖，以景帝始封晉，故為太祖。
value.en: The Jin, because the Xuan King assisted Wei with merit, established him as Gaozu; because the Jing Emperor was first enfeoffed in Jin, he was made Taizu.
value.literal: The Jin, because the Xuan King assisted Wei with merit, established him as Gaozu; because the Jing Emperor was first enfeoffed in Jin, he was made Taizu.

value.zh: 宋氏先世，官閥卑微，雖追崇帝號，劉裕自為高祖。
value.en: The Song clan's earlier generations were of humble official standing; although imperial titles were posthumously conferred, Liu Yu himself served as Gaozu.
value.literal: The Song clan's earlier generations were of humble official standing; although imperial titles were posthumously conferred, Liu Yu himself served as Gaozu.

value.zh: 南齊高帝之父，位至右將軍，生無封爵，不得為太祖，高帝自為太祖。
value.en: The Southern Qi Gaodi's father rose to Right General; in life he received no enfeoffment and could not be Taizu—the Gaodi himself served as Taizu.
value.literal: The Southern Qi Gaodi's father rose to Right General; in life he received no enfeoffment and could not be Taizu—the Gaodi himself served as Taizu.

value.zh: 梁武帝父順之，佐佑齊室，封侯，位至領軍、丹陽尹，雖不受封於梁，亦為太祖。
value.en: Liang Wudi's father Shunzhi assisted the Qi court, was enfeoffed as marquis, and rose to Area Commander and Danyang Intendant; although he received no enfeoffment from Liang, he was made Taizu.
value.literal: Liang Wudi's father Shunzhi assisted the Qi court, was enfeoffed as marquis, and rose to Area Commander and Danyang Intendant; although he received no enfeoffment from Liang, he was made Taizu.

value.zh: 陳武帝父文贊，生無名位，以武帝功，梁室贈侍中，封義興公，及武帝即位，亦追為太祖。
value.en: Chen Wudi's father Wenzan had no rank in life; because of the Wudi's merit, the Liang court posthumously granted him Palace Attendant and enfeoffed him as Duke of Yixing; when the Wudi ascended the throne, he was also posthumously made Taizu.
value.literal: Chen Wudi's father Wenzan had no rank in life; because of the Wudi's merit, the Liang court posthumously granted him Palace Attendant and enfeoffed him as Duke of Yixing; when the Wudi ascended the throne, he was also posthumously made Taizu.

value.zh: 周閔帝以父泰相西魏，經營王業，始封於周，故為太祖。
value.en: Northern Zhou Emperor Min, because his father Tai served as chancellor of Western Wei, built the royal enterprise, and was first enfeoffed in Zhou, made him Taizu.
value.literal: Northern Zhou Emperor Min, because his father Tai served as chancellor of Western Wei and built the royal enterprise and was first enfeoffed in Zhou, made him Taizu.

value.zh: 隋文帝父忠，輔周室有大功，始封於隋，故為太祖。
value.en: Sui Wendi's father Zhong assisted the Zhou court with great merit and was first enfeoffed in Sui; therefore he was made Taizu.
value.literal: Sui Wendi's father Zhong assisted the Zhou court with great merit and was first enfeoffed in Sui; therefore he was made Taizu.

value.zh: 唐高祖神堯祖父虎為周八柱國，隋代追封唐公，故為太祖。
value.en: Tang Gaozu Shenyao's grandfather Hu was one of the Zhou Eight Pillars; the Sui dynasty posthumously enfeoffed him as Duke of Tang; therefore he was made Taizu.
value.literal: Tang Gaozu Shenyao's grandfather Hu was one of the Zhou Eight Pillars; the Sui dynasty posthumously enfeoffed him as Duke of Tang; therefore he was made Taizu.

value.zh: 唐末梁室朱氏有帝位，亦立四廟，朱公先世無名位，雖追冊四廟，不立太祖，朱公自為太祖。
value.en: At the end of Tang the Liang Zhu clan held the imperial throne and also established four temples; the Zhu lord's earlier generations had no rank; although four temples were posthumously enrolled, no Taizu was established—the Zhu lord himself served as Taizu.
value.literal: At the end of Tang the Liang Zhu clan held the imperial throne and also established four temples; the Zhu lord's earlier generations had no rank; although four temples were posthumously enrolled, no Taizu was established—the Zhu lord himself served as Taizu.

value.zh: 此則前代追冊太祖，不出親廟之成例也。
value.en: This shows that in former ages posthumous enrollment as Taizu did not depart from the established precedent of the collateral temples.
value.literal: This shows that in former ages posthumous enrollment as Taizu did not depart from the established precedent of the collateral temples.

value.zh: 張璁
value.en: Zhang Cong
value.literal: Zhang Cong

value.en: (also known as Hu Duo)〉
value.literal: (Hu Duo)〉

value.zh: 桂萼方獻夫夏言
value.en: Gui E, Fang Xianfu, and Xia Yan
value.literal: Gui E, Fang Xianfu, and Xia Yan

value.zh: 未幾，河套議起。
value.en: Before long, the debate over recovering the Ordos arose.
value.literal: Before long, the debate over the Ordos arose.

value.zh: 言故慷慨以經濟自許，思建立不世功。
value.en: Xia Yan had always been ambitious and held himself out as a statesman, intending to win undying distinction.
value.literal: Yan had always been bold and generous, promising himself in statecraft, thinking to establish unprecedented merit.

value.zh: 因陜西總督曾銑請復河套，贊決之。
value.en: When Grand Coordinator Zeng Xian of Shaanxi memorialized for recovering the Ordos, Xia Yan endorsed the proposal.
value.literal: Because Shaanxi Grand Coordinator Zeng Xian requested recovery of the Ordos, he approved and decided it.

value.zh: 嵩與元、炳媒孽其間，竟以此敗。
value.en: Yan Song, together with Cui Yuan and Lu Bing, sowed trouble in the midst of it, and in the end Xia Yan was ruined because of it.
value.literal: Song with Yuan and Bing planted mischief between them; in the end Yan failed because of this.

value.zh: 江都人蘇綱者，言繼妻父也，雅與銑善。
value.en: A man named Su Gang, from Jiangdu, was the father of Xia Yan's second wife and had long been on friendly terms with Zeng Xian.
value.literal: One Su Gang of Jiangdu was Yan's father-in-law by a subsequent wife; he had always been on good terms with Xian.

value.zh: 銑方請復河套，綱亟稱於言。
value.en: While Zeng Xian was pressing his plan to recover the Ordos, Su Gang repeatedly spoke well of him to Xia Yan.
value.literal: When Xian was just requesting recovery of the Ordos, Gang repeatedly praised him to Yan.

value.zh: 言倚銑可辦，密疏薦之，謂群臣無如銑忠者。
value.en: Xia Yan counted on Zeng Xian to see the campaign through and secretly memorialized in his favor, declaring that no minister was more loyal.
value.literal: Yan relied on Xian to be able to accomplish it; secretly memorialized recommending him, saying among the officials none was as loyal as Xian.

value.zh: 帝令言擬旨，優獎之者再。
value.en: The Emperor had Xia Yan draft the rescripts and twice issued him warm commendation.
value.literal: The Emperor ordered Yan to draft rescripts; he commended him with favor twice.

value.zh: 銑喜，益銳意出師。
value.en: Zeng Xian was elated and pressed all the harder to take the field.
value.literal: Xian rejoiced and became even more determined to take the field.

value.zh: 帝忽降旨詰責，語甚厲。
value.en: The Emperor suddenly issued an edict of stern rebuke in the harshest terms.
value.literal: The Emperor suddenly issued an edict of interrogation and rebuke; the language was very severe.

value.zh: 嵩揣知帝意，遂力言河套不可復，語侵言。
value.en: Yan Song read the Emperor's mind and forcefully argued that the Ordos could not be recovered, his words aimed openly at Xia Yan.
value.literal: Song guessed the Emperor's intent and then forcefully argued the Ordos could not be recovered; his words encroached on Yan.

value.zh: 言始大懼，謝罪，且言「嵩未嘗異議，今乃盡諉於臣」。
value.en: Xia Yan was at last deeply alarmed. He apologized and added, "Yan Song never once objected—yet now he lays the entire blame on me."
value.literal: Yan at first was greatly afraid; he apologized and moreover said, "Song never once differed in opinion; now he throws everything on me."

value.zh: 帝責言「強君脅眾」，嵩復騰疏攻言，言亦力辨。
value.en: The Emperor rebuked Xia Yan for "forcing the ruler's hand and browbeating the court." Yan Song followed with another memorial attacking him, and Xia Yan rebutted with equal force.
value.literal: The Emperor rebuked Yan for "forcing the ruler and coercing the multitude"; Song again sent up a memorial attacking Yan, and Yan also vigorously defended himself.

value.zh: 而帝已入嵩譖，怒不可解。
value.en: But the Emperor had already taken Yan Song's accusations to heart, and his rage could not be softened.
value.literal: But the Emperor had already accepted Song's slander; his anger could not be appeased.

value.zh: 二十七年正月盡奪言官階，以尚書致仕，猶無意殺之也。
value.en: In the first month of the twenty-seventh year of the reign, Xia Yan was stripped of all office and permitted to retire as Minister—yet the Emperor still had no wish to kill him.
value.literal: In the first month of year twenty-seven all of Yan's official ranks were stripped; he retired as Minister—but still there was no intent to kill him.

value.zh: 會有蜚語聞禁中，謂言去時怨謗。
value.en: Rumors then reached the inner palace that Xia Yan, on leaving office, had spoken with resentment and slander.
value.literal: There happened to be flying rumors heard within the forbidden precincts, saying Yan when leaving spoke with resentment and slander.

value.zh: 嵩復代仇鸞草奏訐言納銑金，交關為奸利，事連蘇綱，遂下銑、綱詔獄。
value.en: Yan Song then had Qiu Luan draft a memorial accusing Xia Yan of taking bribes from Zeng Xian and trading favors for profit. The case implicated Su Gang, and Zeng Xian and Su Gang were clapped into the imperial prison.
value.literal: Song again had Qiu Luan draft a memorial denouncing Yan for receiving Xian's gold and colluding for corrupt profit; the matter implicated Su Gang; thus Xian and Gang were sent to the imperial prison by edict.

value.zh: 嵩與元、炳謀，坐銑交結近侍律斬，綱戍邊，遣官校逮言。
value.en: Yan Song plotted with Cui Yuan and Lu Bing. Zeng Xian was sentenced to decapitation under the statute on collusion with palace intimates; Su Gang was exiled to the frontier; and officers were sent to seize Xia Yan.
value.literal: Song with Yuan and Bing plotted; Xian was sentenced under the law on collusion with close attendants to decapitation; Gang was exiled to the frontier; official runners were dispatched to arrest Yan.

value.zh: 言抵通州，聞銑所坐，大驚墮車曰：「噫！
value.en: When Xia Yan reached Tongzhou and learned what crime Zeng Xian had been charged with, he was so shaken that he fell from his carriage and cried, "Alas!
value.literal: When Yan reached Tongzhou and heard what Xian was convicted of, he was greatly shocked, fell from his carriage, and said, "Alas!

value.zh: 吾死矣。」
value.en: I am a dead man."
value.literal: I am dead.

value.zh: 再疏訟冤，言：「鸞方就逮，上降諭不兩日，鸞何以知上語，又何知嵩疏而附麗若此？
value.en: He memorialized again to clear his name: "Qiu Luan had only just been placed under arrest. The Emperor's edict is less than two days old—how could Luan already know the Emperor's words? How could he know of Yan Song's memorial and align himself with it in this way?
value.literal: Again memorializing to plead his innocence, he said: "Luan had just been arrested; the Emperor's edict was less than two days ago—how could Luan know the Emperor's words? And how could he know Song's memorial and attach himself like this?

value.zh: 蓋嵩與崔元輩詐為之以傾臣。
value.en: Clearly Yan Song and men like Cui Yuan fabricated this to bring me down.
value.literal: Surely Song with Cui Yuan and company fraudulently made this to overthrow me.

value.zh: 嵩靜言庸違似共工，謙恭下士似王莽，奸巧弄權、父子專政似司馬懿。
value.en: Yan Song's smooth words and treacherous deeds recall Gong Gong; his show of humility toward scholars recalls Wang Mang; his cunning grasp of power and the rule he and his son share recall Sima Yi.
value.literal: Song's quiet speech and outward violation resemble Gong Gong; humble courtesy toward scholars resembles Wang Mang; cunning manipulation of power and father-son monopolizing government resemble Sima Yi.

value.zh: 在內諸臣受其牢籠，知有嵩不知有陛下。
value.en: The ministers within the palace are caught in his net—they know Yan Song, but not Your Majesty.
value.literal: Officials within, subjected to his cage, know Song but do not know Your Majesty.

value.zh: 在外諸臣受其箝制，亦知有嵩不知有陛下。
value.en: The ministers beyond the palace are held under his thumb—they too know Yan Song, but not Your Majesty.
value.literal: Officials without, subjected to his restraint, also know Song but do not know Your Majesty.

value.zh: 臣生死系嵩掌握，惟歸命聖慈，曲賜保全。」
value.en: My life and death rest in Yan Song's hands. I throw myself on Your Majesty's mercy and beg for gracious protection."
value.literal: My life and death hang in Song's grasp; I only entrust myself to holy compassion, beseeching gracious preservation."

value.zh: 帝不省。
value.en: The Emperor paid no heed.
value.literal: The Emperor did not heed.

value.zh: 獄成，刑部尚書喻茂堅、左都御史屠僑等當言死，援議貴議能條以上。
value.en: When the trial concluded, Minister of Justice Yu Maojian, Left Censor-in-Chief Tu Qiao, and others recommended death for Xia Yan, citing the statutes granting leniency to men of rank and ability.
value.literal: When the case was finalized, Minister of Justice Yu Maojian, Left Censor-in-Chief Tu Qiao and others sentenced Yan to death, citing the provisions on officials of merit and talent above.

value.zh: 帝不從，切責茂堅等，奪其俸，猶及言前不戴香冠事。
value.en: The Emperor refused. He sharply rebuked Yu Maojian and the others, docked their salaries, and even revived the old charge that Xia Yan had once failed to wear the incense crown.
value.literal: The Emperor did not agree; he sharply rebuked Yu Maojian and the others and stripped their salaries, also bringing up Yan's earlier failure to wear the incense crown.

value.zh: 其年十月竟棄言市。
value.en: That October Xia Yan was at last executed in the public square.
value.literal: That year in the tenth month Yan was finally executed at the market.

value.zh: 妻蘇流廣西，從子主事克承、從孫尚寶丞朝慶，削籍為民。
value.en: His wife, Lady Su, was banished to Guangxi. His nephew Ke Cheng, a department director, and his grand-nephew Chao Qing, an assistant in the Court of Imperial Studs, were struck from the rolls and reduced to common status.
value.literal: His wife the Su was exiled to Guangxi; his nephew, Department Director Ke Cheng, and grand-nephew, Court of Imperial Studs Assistant Chao Qing, were struck from the registry and made commoners.

value.zh: 言死時年六十有七。
value.en: Xia Yan was sixty-seven when he died.
value.literal: When Yan died he was sixty-seven years old.

value.zh: 劉宗周
value.en: Liu Zongzhou
value.literal: Liu Zongzhou

value.zh: 〈（祝淵王毓蓍）〉
value.en: (Sub-biographies: Zhu Yuan and Wang Yushi)
value.literal: (Zhu Yuan, Wang Yushi)

value.zh: 黃道周
value.en: Huang Daozhou
value.literal: Huang Daozhou

value.zh: 〈（葉廷秀）〉
value.en: (Ye Tingxiu)
value.literal: (Ye Tingxiu)

value.zh: 一曰慎爵賞以肅軍情。
value.en: Third, review ennoblements and rewards carefully to restore military discipline.
value.literal: Third: be cautious with ranks and rewards to stern the military morale.

value.zh: 請分別各帥封賞，孰當孰濫，輕則收侯爵，重則奪伯爵。
value.en: Review every commander's titles and rewards: distinguish the deserved from the gratuitous. Strip lesser offenders of their marquisates; revoke earldoms from the worst.
value.literal: I ask to distinguish the enfeoffments and rewards of each commander—who deserved them and who received them excessively; lightly, strip marquisates; heavily, revoke earldoms.

value.zh: 夫以左帥之恢復而封，高、劉之敗逃亦封，又誰不當封者？
value.en: If the Left Marshal was ennobled for recovering territory while Gao and Liu were rewarded for defeat and flight, who would not claim a title?
value.literal: Now if the Left Marshal was enfeoffed for recovery, while Gao and Liu were also enfeoffed for defeat and flight—who then would not deserve enfeoffment?

value.zh: 武臣既濫，文臣隨之，外臣既濫，中珰隨之，恐天下聞而解體也。
value.en: Indiscriminate rewards to generals invite the same from civil officials, and from regional officials to palace eunuchs. The empire will lose heart when it sees this.
value.literal: Once military ministers are excessive, civil ministers follow; once external ministers are excessive, palace eunuchs follow—I fear the empire will hear of it and disintegrate.

value.zh: 士英大怒，即日具疏辭位，且揚言於朝曰：「劉公自稱草莽孤臣，不書新命，明示不臣天子也。」
value.en: Ma Shi Ying was furious. That same day he submitted his resignation and declared at court: "Lord Liu calls himself a private subject of the wilderness and omitted the new imperial title from his memorial—a plain refusal to acknowledge the Son of Heaven."
value.literal: Shi Ying was greatly enraged; that very day he prepared a memorial resigning his post, and proclaimed in court, saying: "Lord Liu styled himself a lone minister of the wilds and did not write the new appointment—openly showing he will not serve the Son of Heaven."

value.zh: 其私人朱統𨰥遂劾宗周疏請移蹕鳳陽：「鳳陽，高墻所在，欲以罪宗處皇上，而與史可法擁立潞王。
value.en: His client Zhu Tonglei then impeached Zongzhou for requesting that the court move to Fengyang: "Fengyang is a prison city. He means to confine the emperor there while he and Shi Kefa install the Prince of Lu.
value.literal: His private man Zhu Tonglei then impeached Zongzhou's memorial requesting the transfer of the imperial residence to Fengyang: "Fengyang is where high walls stand; he wishes to place the emperor in the place of guilt, and with Shi Kefa to support and establish the Prince of Lu.

value.zh: 其兵已伏丹陽，當急備。」
value.en: His troops are already hidden at Danyang. Guard against them at once."
value.literal: His troops are already lying in ambush at Danyang—urgent preparations should be made."

value.zh: 而澤清、傑日夜謀所以殺宗周者不得，乃遣客十輩往刺宗周。
value.en: Meanwhile Liu Zeqing and Gao Jie plotted day and night to kill Zongzhou. Failing in that, they sent ten groups of assassins after him.
value.literal: Yet Zeqing and Jie day and night schemed how to kill Zongzhou without success; then they sent ten batches of assassins to stab Zongzhou.

value.zh: 宗周時在丹陽，終日危坐，未嘗有惰容，客前後至者，不敢加害而去。
value.en: Zongzhou was then at Danyang, sitting upright all day without a trace of fear. Assassins came and went but none dared strike.
value.literal: Zongzhou was then at Danyang, sitting upright all day, never showing a lazy countenance; assassins who came before and after did not dare harm him and left.

value.zh: 而黃鳴駿入覲，兵抵京口，與防江兵相擊鬥。
value.en: Meanwhile Huang Mingjun came to court, and his troops reached Jingkou and fought with the river-defense forces.
value.literal: Meanwhile Huang Mingjun entered audience; his troops reached Jingkou and clashed with the river-defense troops.

value.zh: 士英以統𨰥言為信也，亦震恐。
value.en: Ma Shi Ying, believing Zhu Tonglei's accusation, was terrified as well.
value.literal: Shi Ying took Tonglei's words as true and was also shaken with terror.

value.zh: 於是澤清疏劾：「宗周陰撓恢復，欲誅臣等，激變士心，召生靈之禍。」
value.en: Then Liu Zeqing memorialized: "Zongzhou secretly sabotages the recovery effort, seeks to execute us, inflames the troops, and invites disaster upon the people."
value.literal: Thus Zeqing memorialized in impeachment: "Zongzhou secretly obstructs recovery, wishes to execute us ministers, stirs mutiny in soldiers' hearts, and summons calamity upon the people."

value.zh: 劉良佐亦具疏言宗周力持「三案」，為門戶主盟，倡議親征，圖晁錯之自為居守，司馬懿之閉城拒君。
value.en: Liu Liangzuo also submitted a memorial accusing Zongzhou of championing the "Three Cases," leading the factional alliance, and urging a personal campaign—plotting, like Chao Cuo, to hold power while the emperor marched, and, like Sima Yi, to shut the gates against the throne.
value.literal: Liu Liangzuo also prepared a memorial saying Zongzhou forcefully upheld the "Three Cases," acted as factional chief, advocated personal campaign, and schemed Chao Cuo's staying behind to hold the fort and Sima Yi's closing the gates to reject the sovereign.

value.zh: 疏未下，澤清復草一疏，署傑、良佐及黃得功名上之，言：「宗周勸上親征，謀危君父，欲安置陛下於烽火兇危之地。
value.en: Before that memorial was even issued, Liu Zeqing drafted another, signed by Gao Jie, Liu Liangzuo, and Huang Degong, declaring: "Zongzhou urged Your Majesty to lead the campaign personally, endangering the throne, and meant to place you in the midst of battle and peril.
value.literal: Before the memorial was issued, Zeqing again drafted a memorial, signed by Jie, Liangzuo, and Huang Degong and submitted it, saying: "Zongzhou urged the sovereign to personally campaign, schemed peril to the sovereign and father, and wished to place Your Majesty in a place of beacon fires and fierce danger.

value.zh: 蓋非宗周一人之謀，姜曰廣、吳甡合謀也。
value.en: This was not Zongzhou's plot alone—Jiang Yueguang and Wu Shen were his co-conspirators.
value.literal: This was not Zongzhou's plot alone—Jiang Yueguang and Wu Shen conspired together.

value.zh: 曰廣心雄膽大，翊戴非其本懷，故陰結死黨，翦除諸忠，然後迫劫乘輿，遷之別郡。
value.en: Yueguang is ambitious and bold; enthroning the emperor was never his true aim. He secretly formed a faction, purged the loyal, and then meant to seize the imperial carriage and relocate the court.
value.literal: Yueguang's heart was bold and his courage great; supporting the enthronement was not his original intent—thus he secretly bound a diehard faction, cut down the loyal, and then coerced the imperial carriage and moved it to another commandery.

value.zh: 如甡、宗周入都，臣等即渡江赴闕，面訐諸奸，正《春秋》討賊之義。」
value.en: If Wu Shen and Zongzhou enter the capital, we shall cross the Yangtze, appear before the throne, denounce these traitors face to face, and uphold the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 principle of punishing rebels."
value.literal: If Shen and Zongzhou enter the capital, we ministers will immediately cross the river and go to the palace, face-to-face denounce the traitors, and uphold the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 righteousness of punishing rebels."

value.zh: 疏入，舉朝大駭，傳諭和衷集事。
value.en: When the memorial arrived, the court was horrified. An edict was issued calling for harmony and unity.
value.literal: When the memorial entered, the whole court was greatly alarmed; an edict was transmitted urging harmony of heart and gathering of affairs.

value.zh: 宗周不得已，以七月十八日入朝。
value.en: Zongzhou had no choice but to enter court on the eighteenth day of the seventh month.
value.literal: Zongzhou had no choice; on the eighteenth day of the seventh month he entered court.

value.zh: 初，澤清疏出，遣人錄示傑。
value.en: When Liu Zeqing's memorial was issued, he sent a copy to Gao Jie.
value.literal: At first, when Zeqing's memorial was issued, he sent someone to copy and show it to Jie.

value.zh: 傑曰：「我輩武人，乃預朝事耶？」
value.en: Gao Jie said: "We are soldiers—since when do we meddle in court affairs?"
value.literal: Jie said: "We military men—are we to participate in court affairs?"

value.zh: 得功疏辨：「臣不預聞。」
value.en: Huang Degong submitted a defense: "Your subject had no part in this."
value.literal: Degong submitted a memorial in defense: "Your subject did not participate in hearing."

value.zh: 士英寢不奏。
value.en: Ma Shi Ying suppressed it and never forwarded it to the throne.
value.literal: Shi Ying shelved it and did not memorialize.

value.zh: 可法不平，遣使遍詰諸鎮，咸云不知，遂據以入告，澤清輩由是氣沮。
value.en: Shi Kefa, indignant, sent envoys to question every garrison. All denied knowledge of the plot. He reported this to the throne, and Liu Zeqing and his allies lost heart.
value.literal: Kefa was indignant; he sent envoys to question all the garrisons everywhere—they all said they did not know—then relied on this to enter and report, and Zeqing and company thereby lost their spirit.

value.zh: 趙倫之蕭思話臧燾
value.en: Zhao Lunzhi, Xiao Sihua, and Zang Dao
value.literal: Zhao Lunzhi, Xiao Sihua, Zang Dao

value.zh: 禮，天子七廟，三昭三穆與太祖而七。
value.en: Ritual: the Son of Heaven has seven temples — three zhao three mu with the Grand Ancestor making seven.
value.literal: Ritual: the Son of Heaven has seven temples — three zhao three mu with the Grand Ancestor making seven.

value.zh: 自考廟以至祖考五廟，皆月祭之。
value.en: From the temple of self-examination to the five temples of ancestors and fathers, all receive monthly sacrifice.
value.literal: From the temple of self-examination to the five temples of ancestors and fathers, all receive monthly sacrifice.

value.zh: 遠廟為祧，有二祧，享嘗乃止。
value.en: The distant temple becomes tiao; there are two tiao; offering and tasting then cease.
value.literal: The distant temple becomes tiao; there are two tiao; offering and tasting then cease.

value.zh: 去祧為壇，去壇為墠，有禱然後祭之，此宗廟之次、親疏之序也。
value.en: Beyond tiao is the altar; beyond the altar is the open ground; when there is prayer then sacrifice is made — this is the order of ancestral temples and the sequence of near and far.
value.literal: Beyond tiao is the altar; beyond the altar is the open ground; when there is prayer then sacrifice is made — this is the order of ancestral temples and the sequence of near and far.

value.zh: 鄭玄以為祧者文王武王之廟，王肅以為五世六世之祖。
value.en: Zheng Xuan held that tiao were the temples of King Wen and King Wu; Wang Su held they were ancestors of the fifth and sixth generations.
value.literal: Zheng Xuan held that tiao were the temples of King Wen and King Wu; Wang Su held they were ancestors of the fifth and sixth generations.

value.zh: 尋去祧之言，則祧非文、武之廟矣。
value.en: Examining the words "beyond tiao," then tiao are not the temples of Wen and Wu.
value.literal: Examining the words "beyond tiao," then tiao are not the temples of Wen and Wu.

value.zh: 文、武，周之祖宗，何雲去祧為壇乎？
value.en: Wen and Wu were Zhou's ancestors — how can one speak of beyond tiao as altar?
value.literal: Wen and Wu were Zhou's ancestors — how can one speak of beyond tiao as altar?

value.zh: 明遠廟為祧者，無服之祖也。
value.en: Clearly the distant temple that becomes tiao is the ancestor beyond mourning.
value.literal: Clearly the distant temple that becomes tiao is the ancestor beyond mourning.

value.zh: 又遠廟則有享嘗之降，去祧則有壇墠之殊，明世遠者其義彌疏也。
value.en: Again for distant temples there is the descent of offering and tasting; beyond tiao there is the difference of altar and open ground — clearly the more distant the generation the more sparse the meaning.
value.literal: Again for distant temples there is the descent of offering and tasting; beyond tiao there is the difference of altar and open ground — clearly the more distant the generation the more sparse the meaning.

value.zh: 若祧是文、武之廟，宜同月祭于太祖，雖推後稷以配天，由功德之所始，非尊崇之義每有差降也。
value.en: If tiao were the temples of Wen and Wu they should like the Grand Ancestor receive monthly sacrifice; though Houji is elevated to match Heaven, that is from the beginning of merit, not that the meaning of honor has difference and descent each time.
value.literal: If tiao were the temples of Wen and Wu they should like the Grand Ancestor receive monthly sacrifice; though Houji is elevated to match Heaven, that is from the beginning of merit, not that the meaning of honor has difference and descent each time.

value.zh: 又禮有以多為貴者，故傳稱「德厚者流光，德薄者流卑」。
value.en: Again ritual has what values the many; therefore tradition says, "Thick virtue shines far; thin virtue flows low."
value.literal: Again ritual has what values the many; therefore tradition says, "Thick virtue shines far; thin virtue flows low."

value.zh: 又言自上以下降殺以兩，禮也。
value.en: Again it says from above to below reduction by twos — that is ritual.
value.literal: Again it says from above to below reduction by twos — that is ritual.

value.zh: 此則尊卑等級之典，上下殊異之文。
value.en: This is the canon of honor and lowliness, the text of difference above and below.
value.literal: This is the canon of honor and lowliness, the text of difference above and below.

value.zh: 而雲天子諸侯俱祭五廟，何哉？
value.en: Yet it says Son of Heaven and feudal lords alike sacrifice at five temples — why?
value.literal: Yet it says Son of Heaven and feudal lords alike sacrifice at five temples — why?

value.zh: 又王祭嫡殤，下及來孫。
value.en: Again the king sacrifices for legitimate early-dead sons, extending down to coming generations.
value.literal: Again the king sacrifices for legitimate early-dead sons, extending down to coming generations.

value.zh: 而上祀之禮不過高祖。
value.en: Yet sacrifice by superiors does not exceed the High Ancestor.
value.literal: Yet sacrifice by superiors does not exceed the High Ancestor.

value.zh: 推隆恩於下流，替誠敬於尊廟，亦非聖人制禮之意也。
value.en: Pushing honor down the stream while replacing sincere reverence at the honored temple — this too is not the sage's intent in making ritual.
value.literal: Pushing honor down the stream while replacing sincere reverence at the honored temple — this too is not the sage's intent in making ritual.

value.zh: 是以泰始建廟，從王氏議，以禮父為士，子為天子諸侯，祭以天子諸侯，其屍服以士服。
value.en: Therefore when Taishi established the temple they followed the Wang clan's argument: by ritual the father is a knight and the son Son of Heaven or feudal lord, yet sacrifice uses Son of Heaven and feudal lord while the corpse's garment uses knight's garment.
value.literal: Therefore when Taishi established the temple they followed the Wang clan's argument: by ritual the father is a knight and the son Son of Heaven or feudal lord, yet sacrifice uses Son of Heaven and feudal lord while the corpse's garment uses knight's garment.

value.zh: 故上及征西，以備六世之數。
value.en: Thus upstream to Pacifying the West, to complete the number of six generations.
value.literal: Thus upstream to Pacifying the West, to complete the number of six generations.

value.zh: 宣皇雖為太祖，尚在子孫之位，至於殷祭之日，未申東向之禮，所謂子雖齊聖，不先父食者矣。
value.en: Emperor Xuan though Grand Ancestor was still in the place of descendants; on the day of the great offering he had not yet received the east-facing rite — what is called though the son equals sainthood he does not eat before the father.
value.literal: Emperor Xuan though Grand Ancestor was still in the place of descendants; on the day of the great offering he had not yet received the east-facing rite — what is called though the son equals sainthood he does not eat before the father.

value.zh: 今京兆以上既遷，太祖始得居正，議者以昭穆未足，欲屈太祖于卑坐，臣以為非禮典之旨也。
value.en: Now that Jingzhao and above have moved, the Grand Ancestor at last occupies the correct place; debaters, because zhao and mu are not full, wish to bend the Grand Ancestor to the low seat — your servant holds this is not the intent of ritual canon.
value.literal: Now that Jingzhao and above have moved, the Grand Ancestor at last occupies the correct place; debaters, because zhao and mu are not full, wish to bend the Grand Ancestor to the low seat — your servant holds this is not the intent of ritual canon.

value.zh: 所謂與太祖而七，自是昭穆既足，太廟在六世之外，非為須滿七廟乃得居太祖也。
value.en: What is called "with the Grand Ancestor making seven" is itself that zhao and mu are already full and the Grand Temple lies outside the six generations — not that one must fill seven temples before the Grand Ancestor may occupy that place.
value.literal: What is called "with the Grand Ancestor making seven" is itself that zhao and mu are already full and the Grand Temple lies outside the six generations — not that one must fill seven temples before the Grand Ancestor may occupy that place.

value.zh: 議者又以四府君神主，宜永同于殷祫。
value.en: Debaters also held the spirit tablets of the four lords should forever share the great offering like the yin sacrifice.
value.literal: Debaters also held the spirit tablets of the four lords should forever share the great offering like the yin sacrifice.

value.zh: 臣又以為不然。
value.en: Your servant again holds this is not so.
value.literal: Your servant again holds this is not so.

value.zh: 傳所謂毀廟之主，陳乎太祖，謂太祖以下先君之主也。
value.en: Tradition speaks of the destroyed temple's tablet displayed before the Grand Ancestor — meaning the tablets of former lords below the Grand Ancestor.
value.literal: Tradition speaks of the destroyed temple's tablet displayed before the Grand Ancestor — meaning the tablets of former lords below the Grand Ancestor.

value.zh: 故白虎通云：「禘祫祭遷廟者，以其繼君之體，持其統而不絕也。」
value.en: Therefore the Baihu Tong says, "The di and ha sacrifices move destroyed temples because they continue the lord's body and hold the line without breaking."
value.literal: Therefore the Baihu Tong says, "The di and ha sacrifices move destroyed temples because they continue the lord's body and hold the line without breaking."

value.zh: 豈如四府君在太祖之前乎，非繼統之主，無靈命之瑞，非王業之基。
value.en: How could the four lords be before the Grand Ancestor? They are not lords who continue the line, have no auspicious mandate, are not the foundation of royal enterprise.
value.literal: How could the four lords be before the Grand Ancestor? They are not lords who continue the line, have no auspicious mandate, are not the foundation of royal enterprise.

value.zh: 昔以世近而及，今則情禮已遠，而當長饗殷祫，永虛太祖之位，求之禮籍。
value.en: Formerly because the generation was near they were included; now feeling and ritual are already far — yet they should long enjoy the great yin offering and forever leave the Grand Ancestor's place empty; seeking this in ritual texts —
value.literal: Formerly because the generation was near they were included; now feeling and ritual are already far — yet they should long enjoy the great yin offering and forever leave the Grand Ancestor's place empty; seeking this in ritual texts —

value.zh: 未見其可。
value.en: one does not see that it may be done.
value.literal: one does not see that it may be done.

value.zh: 昔永和之初，大議斯禮，于時虞喜、范宣並以洪儒碩學，咸謂四府君神主無緣永存於百世。
value.en: Formerly at the beginning of Yonghe there was great debate on this ritual; at that time Yu Xi and Fan Xuan, both great Confucian scholars, all held the four lords' spirit tablets had no reason to remain forever for a hundred generations.
value.literal: Formerly at the beginning of Yonghe there was great debate on this ritual; at that time Yu Xi and Fan Xuan, both great Confucian scholars, all held the four lords' spirit tablets had no reason to remain forever for a hundred generations.

value.zh: 或欲瘞之兩階，或欲藏之石室，或欲為之改築，雖所執小異，而大歸是同。
value.en: Some wished to bury them at the two steps, some to store them in a stone chamber, some to rebuild for them — though what they held differed in small ways the great direction was the same.
value.literal: Some wished to bury them at the two steps, some to store them in a stone chamber, some to rebuild for them — though what they held differed in small ways the great direction was the same.

value.zh: 若宣皇既居群廟之上，而四主禘祫不已，則大晉殷祭長無太祖之位矣。
value.en: If Emperor Xuan already stands above the group of temples and the four lords' di and ha offerings never cease, then Great Jin's great yin sacrifice would forever lack the Grand Ancestor's place.
value.literal: If Emperor Xuan already stands above the group of temples and the four lords' di and ha offerings never cease, then Great Jin's great yin sacrifice would forever lack the Grand Ancestor's place.

value.zh: 夫理貴有中，不必過厚，禮與世遷，豈可順而不斷？
value.en: Principle values the mean — one need not exceed in thickness; ritual moves with the age — how can one follow without deciding?
value.literal: Principle values the mean — one need not exceed in thickness; ritual moves with the age — how can one follow without deciding?

value.zh: 故臣子之情雖篤，而靈、厲之諡彌彰，追遠之懷雖切，而遷毀之禮為用。
value.en: Thus though ministers' and sons' feeling is deep, the posthumous titles of Ling and Li grow ever clearer; though longing for the distant is keen, the ritual of transfer and destruction is what applies.
value.literal: Thus though ministers' and sons' feeling is deep, the posthumous titles of Ling and Li grow ever clearer; though longing for the distant is keen, the ritual of transfer and destruction is what applies.

value.zh: 豈不有心于加厚，顧禮制不可踰耳。
value.en: Is it not that the heart wishes to add thickness but ritual system cannot be overstepped?
value.literal: Is it not that the heart wishes to add thickness but ritual system cannot be overstepped?

value.zh: 石室則藏於廟北，改築則未知所處。
value.en: Stone chamber means storing north of the temple; rebuilding means not knowing where to place them.
value.literal: Stone chamber means storing north of the temple; rebuilding means not knowing where to place them.

value.zh: 虞主所以依神，神移則有瘞埋之禮。
value.en: The yu tablet exists to rely on the spirit; when the spirit moves there is the ritual of burial.
value.literal: The yu tablet exists to rely on the spirit; when the spirit moves there is the ritual of burial.

value.zh: 四主若饗祀宜廢，亦神之所不依也。
value.en: If the four lords' offering sacrifice should be abolished, that too is what the spirit does not rely on.
value.literal: If the four lords' offering sacrifice should be abolished, that too is what the spirit does not rely on.

value.zh: 准傍事例，宜同虞主之瘞埋。
value.en: Following parallel cases one should like the yu tablet's burial.
value.literal: Following parallel cases one should like the yu tablet's burial.

value.zh: 然經典難詳，群言錯繆，非臣淺識所能折中。
value.en: Yet the classics are hard to detail and many words err — this is not what your servant's shallow understanding can reconcile.
value.literal: Yet the classics are hard to detail and many words err — this is not what your servant's shallow understanding can reconcile.

value.zh: 時學者多從燾議，竟未施行。
value.en: At that time most scholars followed Dao's argument; in the end it was not implemented.
value.literal: At that time most scholars followed Dao's argument; in the end it was not implemented.

value.zh: 文皇帝諱丕，字子桓，武帝太子也。
value.en: Emperor Wen—whose personal name was Pi and courtesy name Zihuan—was the heir apparent of Emperor Wu (Cao Cao).
value.literal: Emperor Wen, taboo name Pi, courtesy name Zihuan, was the heir son of Emperor Wu.

value.zh: 中平四年冬，生于譙。
value.en: He was born at Qiao in the winter of the fourth year of the Zhongping era (187 CE).
value.literal: In the winter of the fourth year of Zhongping, he was born in Qiao.

value.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：帝生時，有雲氣青色而圜如車盖當其上，終日，望氣者以爲至貴之證，非人臣之氣。
value.en: 〈The Wei Book records that at his birth a greenish aura hung above him in a disk like a carriage canopy for the whole day; diviners of qi pronounced it the sign of supreme eminence—not the kind of portent that attends an ordinary minister.
value.literal: 〈The Wei Book says: When the Emperor was born, there was green cloud vapor, round like a carriage canopy, suspended above him all day; those who read auspicious vapors took it as proof of the utmost nobility, not the aura of a mere subject.

value.zh: 年八歲，能屬文。
value.en: At eight he could already write polished compositions.
value.literal: At age eight, he could compose connected literary pieces.

value.zh: 有逸才，遂博貫古今經傳諸子百家之書。
value.en: Gifted with extraordinary ability, he went on to command the classics and their commentaries and the writings of the hundred schools past and present.
value.literal: He had outstanding talent, and thereupon broadly mastered the classics and commentaries and the writings of the hundred schools from ancient to modern times.

value.zh: 善騎射，好擊劔。
value.en: He excelled at horsemanship and archery and delighted in swordplay.
value.literal: He was skilled at riding and archery, and fond of fencing.

value.zh: 舉茂才，不行。
value.en: Nominated as a "flourishing talent," he declined to serve.
value.literal: He was recommended as a maocai (flourishing talent), but did not take office.

value.zh: 《獻帝起居注》曰：建安十五年，爲司徒趙溫所辟。
value.en: According to the Daily Records of Emperor Xian, in Jian'an 15 (210 CE) he was recruited by Minister of Education Zhao Wen.
value.literal: The Daily Records of Emperor Xian says: In the fifteenth year of Jian'an, he was summoned by Minister of Education Zhao Wen.

value.zh: 太祖表「溫辟臣子弟，選舉故不以實」。
value.en: The Grand Progenitor memorialized: "Zhao Wen has summoned my sons and younger relatives; therefore the selection is not according to reality."
value.literal: The Grand Progenitor memorialized: "Zhao Wen has summoned my sons and younger relatives; therefore the selection is not according to reality."

value.zh: 使侍中守光祿勳郗慮持節奉策免溫官。〉
value.en: He had Palace Attendant and acting Supervisor of the Household Xi Lu carry the credential and deliver the edict stripping Zhao Wen of his post.〉
value.literal: He ordered Palace Attendant acting Supervisor of the Household Xi Lu, bearing the insignia, to present the edict and dismiss Zhao Wen from office.〉

value.zh: 建安十六年，爲五官中郎將、副丞相。
value.en: In Jian'an 16 (211 CE) he was appointed General of the Household for All Purposes and deputy to the Chancellor.
value.literal: In the sixteenth year of Jian'an, he became General of the Household for All Purposes and deputy to the Chancellor.

value.zh: 二十二年，立爲魏太子。
value.en: In the twenty-second year of Jian'an (217 CE) he was named heir apparent of Wei.
value.literal: In the twenty-second year, he was established as heir apparent of Wei.

value.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：太祖不時立太子，太子自疑。
value.en: 〈The Wei Summary notes that Cao Cao had long delayed naming an heir, and the crown prince began to doubt his position.
value.literal: 〈The Wei Summary says: The Grand Progenitor did not promptly establish an heir apparent; the heir apparent himself grew doubtful.

value.zh: 是時有高元呂者，善相人，乃呼問之，對曰：「其貴乃不可言。」
value.en: There was a physiognomist named Gao Yuanlü whom Pi summoned and questioned; Gao answered, "The degree of eminence is beyond words."
value.literal: At this time there was a man named Gao Yuanlü who was skilled at physiognomy; he was summoned and asked, and replied: "His nobility cannot be described in words."

value.zh: 問：「壽幾何？」
value.en: Pi asked, "How long will he live?"
value.literal: He was asked: "How long will his lifespan be?"

value.zh: 元呂曰：「其壽，至四十當有小苦，過是無憂也。」
value.en: Gao Yuanlü replied, "He will meet a brief ordeal at forty; after that, nothing to fear."
value.literal: Yuanlü said: "As for his lifespan, when he reaches forty there will be a small hardship; beyond that there will be no worries."

value.zh: 後無幾而立爲王太子，至年四十而薨。〉
value.en: Soon afterward Pi was installed as heir apparent of the King of Wei; he died in his fortieth year.
value.literal: Not long afterward he was established as heir apparent of the king; he reached age forty and died.

value.zh: 太祖崩，嗣位爲丞相、魏王。
value.en: When Cao Cao died, Pi succeeded him as Chancellor and King of Wei.
value.literal: The Grand Progenitor died; he succeeded to the posts of Chancellor and King of Wei.

value.zh: 〈袁宏《漢紀》載漢帝詔曰：「魏太子丕：昔皇天授乃顯考以翼我皇家，遂攘除羣凶，拓定九州，弘功茂績，光于宇宙，朕用垂拱負扆二十有餘載。
value.en: 〈Yuan Hong's Han Annals preserves an imperial edict: "Heir apparent Pi of Wei: High Heaven once entrusted your late father to uphold Our house; he crushed the rebels, pacified the Nine Regions, and left achievements that fill heaven and earth—while I, leaning on the cushions at court, reigned at ease for more than twenty years.
value.literal: 〈Yuan Hong's Han Annals carries an edict of the Han Emperor: "Wei heir apparent Pi: Formerly August Heaven entrusted your illustrious father to aid Our royal house; thereupon he swept away the multitude of villains and expanded and settled the Nine Provinces; his grand merit and abundant deeds shine through the universe; I therefore leaned on the rail with folded arms for more than twenty years.

value.zh: 天不憖遺一老，永保余一人，早世潛神，哀悼傷切。
value.en: Heaven would not spare one wise elder to shelter Me alone; he left the world too soon, and My sorrow cuts deep.
value.literal: Heaven is not willing to leave Us one elder to forever protect Us alone; he departed the world early and concealed his spirit; Our grief and mourning are cutting.

value.zh: 丕奕世宣明，宜秉文武，紹熙前緒。
value.en: Pi carries forward a luminous succession; he should wield both civil and military authority and carry on the work begun before him.
value.literal: Pi in successive generations shines brightly; he should grasp civil and military affairs and continue and brighten the former threads.

value.zh: 今使使持節御史大夫華歆奉策詔授丕丞相印綬、魏王璽紱，領冀州牧。
value.en: I therefore dispatch Bearer of the Imperial Insignia and Imperial Counselor Hua Xin to deliver the edict investing Pi with the Chancellor's seal and ribbon, the regalia of the King of Wei, and the governorship of Ji Province.
value.literal: Now sending Bearer of the Imperial Insignia Imperial Counselor Hua Xin to present by edict and confer on Pi the Chancellor's seal-cord, the King of Wei's seal and ribbon, and headship as Governor of Ji Province.

value.zh: 方今外有遺虜，遐夷未賔，旗鼓猶在邊境，干戈不得韜刃，斯乃播揚洪烈，立功垂名之秋也。
value.en: Barbarians still linger beyond the frontiers, distant peoples have not yet come to court, signal drums stand posted along the borders, and arms cannot yet be laid aside—this is the very hour to broadcast great deeds and win lasting fame.
value.literal: At present beyond Us there remain remnant barbarians; distant tribes have not yet submitted; banners and drums are still at the borders; weapons cannot sheath their blades—this is indeed the autumn season for spreading abroad mighty deeds and establishing merit to leave a name.

value.zh: 豈得脩諒闇之禮，究曾、閔之志哉？
value.en: How could you confine yourself to solitary mourning like a common heir or imitate only the filial retreats of Zengzi and Min Ziqian?
value.literal: How can one observe the rites of silent mourning in the dark chamber and exhaust the intentions of Zeng and Min?

value.zh: 其敬服朕命，抑弭憂懷，旁祗厥緒，時亮庶功，以稱朕意。
value.en: Therefore obey this charge with reverence: set anxiety aside, uphold the legacy on every side, and in due course bring every task to fruition, that My wishes may be fulfilled.
value.literal: Respectfully obey Our command; suppress and extinguish anxious thoughts; broadly reverence its continuation; seasonally brighten the various achievements, thereby matching Our intention.

value.zh: 於戲，可不勉與！」〉
value.en: Ah—how could you do otherwise than strive with all your might!"〉"
value.literal: Alas, can you not exert yourself!"〉"

value.zh: 尊王后曰王太后。
value.en: The queen consort was elevated to Queen Dowager of Wei.
value.literal: The queen consort was honored as Queen Dowager of the King.

value.zh: 改建安二十五年爲延康元年。
value.en: The twenty-fifth year of Jian'an was redesignated the first year of the Yan Kang era (220 CE).
value.literal: He changed the twenty-fifth year of Jian'an to be the first year of Yan Kang.

value.zh: 六年春二月，遣使者循行許昌以東盡沛郡，問民所疾苦，貧者振貸之。
