value.en: In the second month of spring of the sixth year inspectors toured from Xuchang east through Pei commandery, inquiring after hardships and granting grain loans to the poor.
value.literal: Sixth year spring second month, dispatched envoys touring east of Xuchang to reach Pei commandery, asking people what bitter ailments; poor ones relieved lent them.

value.zh: 〈《魏略》載詔曰：「昔軒轅建四面之號，周武稱『予有亂臣十人』，斯蓋先聖所以體國君民，亮成天工，多賢爲貴也。
value.en: 〈The Wei Summary preserves an edict: "The Yellow Emperor posted advisers on four sides; King Wu spoke of ten ministers who could cure chaos—because sage rulers cherish worthy ministers when ordering state and heaven's task alike.
value.literal: 〈Wei Summary carries edict saying: "Formerly Xuanyuan established four-side titles; Zhou Wu called 'I have disorder ministers ten persons'—this covers former sages thereby embodying state ruling people, bright completing heavenly work, many worthies as noble.

value.zh: 今內有公卿以鎮京師，外設牧伯以監四方，至於元戎出征，則軍中宜有柱石之賢帥，輜重所在，又宜有鎮守之重臣，然後車駕可以周行天下，無內外之慮。
value.en: At court ministers stabilize Luoyang; in the regions governors watch the corners—when the supreme commander campaigns there must be stalwart generals in the field and trustworthy ministers guarding supply lines; only then can the emperor journey safely without dread inside or out.
value.literal: Now inside have dukes and ministers to guard capital city; outside establish shepherds and elders to supervise four quarters—as for commander-in-chief going campaign, then army center ought have pillar-stone worthy commander; baggage trains located place, again ought have guarding heavy ministers—then afterward imperial carriage can circle journey all-under-heaven, without internal-external worries.

value.zh: 吾今當征賊，欲守之積年。
value.en: I am about to strike the rebels and expect the duty to last several years.
value.literal: I now about to campaign rebels, wish guard them accumulated years.

value.zh: 其以尚書令潁鄉侯陳羣爲鎮軍大將軍，尚書僕射西鄉侯司馬懿爲撫軍大將軍。
value.en: Chen Qun, Marquis of Yingxiang, is named General Who Guards the Army, and Sima Yi, Marquis of Xixiang, General Who Pacifies the Army.
value.literal: Let Supervisor of the Secretariat Yingxiang Marquis Chen Qun be General Who Guards the Army; Deputy Director of the Secretariat Xixiang Marquis Sima Yi be General Who Pacifies the Army.

value.zh: 若吾臨江授諸將方略，則撫軍當留許昌，督後諸軍，錄後臺文書事；
value.en: If I take the front line to brief the generals, the Pacification general stays in Xuchang to coordinate rear echelons and handle secretariat paperwork;
value.literal: If I along river grant generals plans, then Pacify Army should remain Xuchang, supervise rear various armies, record rear platform document affairs;

value.zh: 鎮軍隨車駕，當董督衆軍，錄行尚書事；
value.en: the general who guards the army escorts the throne, commands the host, and holds traveling authority as head of the secretariat;
value.literal: Guard Army follows imperial carriage, should superintend oversee host of armies, record traveling Supervisor of Secretariat affairs;

value.zh: 皆假節鼓吹，給中軍兵騎六百人。
value.en: each receives the credential, musicians, and six hundred guards from the central army.
value.literal: all lent credential drum-blow, supply center army soldiers cavalry six hundred men.

value.zh: 吾欲去江數里，築宮室，往來其中，見賊可擊之形，便出奇兵擊之；
value.en: I will build a redoubt a few li from the river, move between it and the camp, and when the enemy offers a target I will sally with picked troops;
value.literal: I wish go several li from river, build palace rooms, go-come within them, see enemy can strike form, then issue strange troops strike them;

value.zh: 若或未可，則當舒六軍以遊獵，饗賜軍士。」〉
value.en: if no opening appears I will exercise the six armies on hunt maneuvers and feast the troops."〉"
value.literal: if or not yet possible, then should extend six armies to roam hunt, feast bestow soldiers."〉"

value.zh: 三月，行幸召陵，通討虜渠。
value.en: In March he visited Shaoling and reopened the Taolu canal.
value.literal: Third month, progressed favor Shaoling, opened Taolu canal.

value.zh: 乙巳，還許昌宮。
value.en: On the yisi day he returned to Xuchang Palace.
value.literal: Yisi, returned Xuchang Palace.

value.zh: 并州刺史梁習討鮮卑軻比能，大破之。
value.en: Liang Xi, inspector of Bing province, attacked the Xianbei chief Kebineng and routed him.
value.literal: Bing Province Inspector Liang Xi campaigned against Xianbei Ke Bineng, greatly defeated him.

value.zh: 辛未，帝爲舟師東征。
value.en: On the xinwei day the emperor led the river fleet east.
value.literal: Xinwei, Emperor made naval army east campaign.

value.zh: 五月戊申，幸譙。
value.en: On the wushen day in the fifth month he visited Qiao.
value.literal: Fifth month Wushen, favored Qiao.

value.zh: 壬戌，熒惑入太微。
value.en: On the renxu day Mars entered the Supreme Palace enclosure.
value.literal: Renxu, Sparkling Deluder entered Supreme Subtlety.

value.zh: 七年春正月，將幸許昌，許昌城南門無故自崩，帝心惡之，遂不入。
value.en: In the first month of spring of the seventh year he meant to visit Xuchang, but the south gate collapsed without cause; taking it as an ill omen he turned back.
value.literal: Seventh year spring first month, about to favor Xuchang—Xuchang city south gate without cause self collapsed—Emperor heart loathed it—thereupon did not enter.

value.zh: 壬子，行還洛陽宮。
value.en: On the renzi day he returned to Luoyang Palace.
value.literal: Renzi, progressed returned Luoyang Palace.

value.zh: 三月，築九華臺。
value.en: In March he built the Nine Splendors Terrace.
value.literal: Third month, built Nine Splendor Terrace.

value.zh: 夏五月丙辰，帝疾篤，召中軍大將軍曹真、鎮軍大將軍陳羣、征東大將軍曹休、撫軍大將軍司馬宣王，並受遺詔輔嗣主。
value.en: On bingchen in the fifth month of summer, when the emperor’s illness was grave, he summoned Grand General of the Central Army Cao Zhen, Grand General Who Guards the Army Chen Qun, Grand General Who Campaigns East Cao Xiu, and Grand General Who Pacifies the Army Sima Yi; all received the testamentary edict to assist the succeeding ruler.
value.literal: Summer fifth month Bingchen, Emperor illness severe—summoned Central Army Grand General Cao Zhen, Guard Army Grand General Chen Qun, East Campaign Grand General Cao Xiu, Pacify Army Grand General Sima Xuanwang—all received testament edict assisting heir lord.

value.zh: 遣後宮淑媛、昭儀已下歸其家。
value.en: Concubines ranked gentle ladies and below were sent home to their families.
value.literal: Dispatched rear palace Shuyuan, Zhaoyi and below return their homes.

value.zh: 丁巳，帝崩于嘉福殿，時年四十。
value.en: On the dingsi day he died in Jiafu Hall at the age of forty.
value.literal: Dingsi, Emperor collapsed at Jiafu Hall, age then forty.

value.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：殯於崇華前殿。〉
value.en: 〈The Wei Book states that his bier rested in the front hall of Chonghua.
value.literal: 〈Wei Book says: Laying out at Chonghua Front Hall.

value.zh: 六月戊寅，葬首陽陵。
value.en: On the wuyin day in the sixth month he was buried at Shouyang Mausoleum.
value.literal: Sixth month Wuyin, buried Shouyang Mausoleum.

value.zh: 自殯及葬，皆以終制從事。
value.en: From lying in state to interment every rite followed his own austere "final instructions."
value.literal: From laying out to burial, all by final regulations conducted affairs.

value.zh: 〈《魏氏春秋》曰：明帝將送葬，曹真、陳羣、王朗等以暑熱固諫，乃止。
value.en: 〈The Wei shi chunqiu notes that Emperor Ming meant to join the funeral train but Cao Zhen, Chen Qun, Wang Lang, and others dissuaded him in the sweltering heat—so he desisted.
value.literal: 〈Wei Family Spring and Autumn says: Ming Di was about to escort burial—Cao Zhen, Chen Qun, Wang Lang etc. by summer heat firmly remonstrated—then stopped.

value.zh: 孫盛曰：夫窀穸之事，孝子之極痛也，人倫之道，於斯莫重。
value.en: Sun Sheng remarks that laying a parent to rest is the filial son's sharpest grief—nothing weightier in human duty.
value.literal: Sun Sheng says: As for burial vault affairs—filial son's utmost pain; human relations way—here nothing heavier.

value.zh: 故天子七月而葬，同軌畢至。
value.en: Hence the emperor waits seven months for burial so every carriage track may converge.
value.literal: Therefore Son of Heaven seventh month then bury—same track all arrive.

value.zh: 夫以義感之情，猶盡臨隧之哀，況乎天性發中，敦禮者重之哉！
value.en: Even ritual bonds demand the full grief at the grave—how much more the bond of nature for those who prize propriety!
value.literal: By righteousness-moved feelings—still exhaust overseeing tunnel grief—how much more heavenly nature issuing center—those who esteem ritual value it!

value.zh: 魏氏之德，仍世不基矣。
value.en: Such thin virtue ill suits lasting foundations for the house of Wei.
value.literal: Wei clan's virtue—still generations not foundation.

value.zh: 昔華元厚葬，君子以爲棄君於惡，羣等之諫，棄孰甚焉！
value.en: Long ago Hua Yuan gave a lavish funeral; the nobles read it as abandoning his lord to wrong—what greater betrayal than Chen Qun's counsel to stay away?
value.literal: Formerly Hua Yuan thick burial—gentleman thought abandoned lord in evil—Qun etc.'s remonstrance—abandonance which more extreme!

value.zh: 鄄城侯植爲誄曰：「惟黃初七年五月七日，大行皇帝崩，嗚呼哀哉！
value.en: The Marquis of Juancheng, Cao Zhi, composed a dirge: "On the seventh day of the fifth month of Huangchu seven (226 CE) the late emperor passed away—alas, the sorrow!
value.literal: Marquis of Juancheng Zhi composed a dirge saying: "Only Huangchu seventh year fifth month seventh day, the Grand Procession Emperor collapsed—alas, how bitter is our grief!

value.zh: 于時天震地駭，崩山隕霜，陽精薄景，五緯錯行，百姓呼嗟，萬國悲悼，若喪考妣，恩過墓唐，擗踊郊野，仰想穹蒼，僉曰何辜，早世殞喪，嗚呼哀哉！
value.en: Heaven trembled and earth reeled; peaks shattered and frost fell; the sun's fire dimmed; the five planets left their tracks; people wailed and every polity grieved as for lost parents; kindness deeper than at Tang's tomb; mourners beat their breasts in the outer suburbs and scanned the sky—why must guilt strike him who died before his time? Alas, the sorrow!
value.literal: Then Heaven quaked and Earth was shaken; mountains split and frost fell; the sun's essence thinned its glory; the five planetary traces ran awry; the hundred surnames cried aloud; the myriad regions mourned—as mourning father and mother; kindness surpassed tomb-site Tang; beating breasts and stamping in the suburban wilds; looking up pondering deep azure—all said what guilt—early age perished loss—alas, how bitter is our grief!

value.zh: 悲夫大行，忽焉光滅，永棄萬國，雲往雨絕。
value.en: Alas for the departed sovereign—his light snuffed in an instant, forever lost to the realm; clouds have fled and the rains ceased.
value.literal: Alas for Grand Procession—suddenly radiance extinguished; forever cast off from myriad regions; clouds gone rain cut off.

value.zh: 承問荒忽，惛懵哽咽，袖鋒抽刃，歎自僵斃，追慕三良，甘心同穴。
value.en: When the news reached me I reeled in confusion, voice choked—I would have drawn steel and struck myself down; I envied the three Good Men who followed Duke Mu into death and wished to share one tomb.
value.literal: Receiving tidings wild confused, dark dull choking—sleeve blade draw dagger—sigh self rigid death—long for Three Good Men—glad heart same cave.

value.zh: 感惟南風，惟以鬱滯，終於偕沒，指景自誓。
value.en: The south wind stirs grief still pent within us—we shall perish together; I swear by the moving sun.
value.literal: Moved only south wind—only thereby pent stagnant—in end together perish—point shadow self swear.

value.zh: 考諸先記，尋之哲言，生若浮寄，惟德可論，朝聞夕逝，孔志所存。
value.en: Ancient texts and wise men taught that life is fleeting lodging and only virtue endures; "hear the Way at dawn, die content at dusk"—such was Confucius's pledge.
value.literal: Examine various former records—trace them sage words—life like floating lodging—only virtue can be discussed—dawn hear dusk depart—Kong resolve stored.

value.zh: 皇雖一沒，天祿永延，何以述德？
value.en: Though he has passed in one stroke, Heaven's blessing flows onward—how shall we proclaim his merit?
value.literal: Sovereign though once gone—Heaven salary forever extended—how thereby narrate virtue?

value.zh: 表之素旃。
value.en: We inscribe it on the white funeral banner.
value.literal: Display them plain white banners.

value.zh: 何以詠功？
value.en: How shall we sing his achievements?
value.literal: How thereby chant merit?

value.zh: 宣之管絃。
value.en: Let pipes and strings carry them abroad.
value.literal: Proclaim them pipes strings.

value.zh: 乃作誄曰：皓皓太素，兩儀始分，中和產物，肈有人倫，爰曁三皇，寔秉道真，降逮五帝，繼以懿純，三代製作，踵武立勳。
value.en: The dirge continues: "Bright primal purity split into yin and yang and yielded the human order; the Three Sovereigns grasped the true Dao, the Five Thearchs followed in unstained line, and the Three Dynasties built institutions and trod the path of merit.
value.literal: Thus composing dirge says: Bright bright Great Simplicity—two powers first divided—center harmony produced creatures—thereupon human relations—then reaching Three August Ones—truly grasped Way true—descending reaching Five Thearchs—in succession with pure grace—Three Ages fashioned institutions—heel-print martial raised merit.

value.zh: 季嗣不維，網漏于秦，崩樂滅學，儒坑禮焚，二世而殲，漢氏乃因，弗求古訓，嬴政是遵，王綱帝典，闃爾無聞。
value.en: Successors failed their bond; Qin's net tore—music fell and learning died, Confucians were buried and ritual texts burned; Er Shi fell within two reigns. Han arose yet spurned antique teaching and copied the First Emperor until royal norms seemed lost in silence.
value.literal: Later heirs not bind—net leaked under Qin—collapse music destroy learning—Ru buried ritual burned—Second Generation then destroyed—Han clan thereupon continued—not seeking ancient instructions—Ying Zheng this followed—kingly cord imperial canon—silent indeed unheard.

value.zh: 末光幽昧，道究運遷，乾坤迴歷，簡聖授賢，乃眷大行，屬以黎元。
value.en: Twilight deepened until fortune shifted; heaven and earth rolled through cycles until the canon chose sages—and then He turned to the late emperor and entrusted him with the black-haired masses.
value.literal: Last gleam dark dim—Way exhausted fortune shift—Qian Kun circuit rounds—select sage grant worthy—then favor Grand Procession—entrust with black-haired masses.

value.zh: 龍飛啟祚，合契上玄，五行定紀，改號革年，明明赫赫，受命于天。
value.en: The dragon throne rose, cosmic tallies aligned with High Heaven, the Five Agents received their stations, reign titles and years were renewed—radiant and august, he bore Heaven's mandate.
value.literal: Dragon fly open fortune—combine tally Upper Dark—Five Phases fix records—change designation reform year—bright bright blazing blazing—receive mandate from Heaven.

value.zh: 仁風偃物，德以禮宣；
value.en: His humane breezes bowed all creation; his power moved through ritual;
value.literal: Humane wind lay things low—virtue by ritual proclaimed;

value.zh: 祥惟聖質，嶷在幼妍。
value.en: augury marked his sacred nature, steadfast even in childhood grace.
value.literal: Auspicious only sage substance—towering in youth grace.

value.zh: 庻幾六典，學不過庭，潛心無罔，亢志青冥。
value.en: He aspired to the Six Canons, studied within his courtyard, pondered without guile, and raised his purpose toward the empyrean.
value.literal: Almost Six Canons—learning not passing courtyard—sink heart without deceit—raise resolve blue-dark.

value.zh: 才秀藻朗，如玉之瑩，聽察無嚮，瞻覩未形。
value.en: Talent shone clear as polished jade; his hearing needed no prompting, his sight pierced what had not yet taken shape.
value.literal: Talent splendid polish bright—like jade's luster—hearing examining without direction—gazing seeing unformed.

value.zh: 其剛如金，其貞如瓊，如氷之絜，如砥之平。
value.en: He was hard as metal, constant as jade, pure as ice, level as a whetstone.
value.literal: His hardness like gold—his constancy like fine jade—like ice's purity—like whetstone's level.

value.zh: 爵公無私，戮違無輕，心鏡萬機，攬照下情。
value.en: He enfeoffed without favoritism and punished rebels without laxity; his mind mirrored every policy and illumined the people's plight.
value.literal: Ennobling dukes without selfishness—punishing rebels without lightness—heart mirrors myriad mechanisms—gather shine lower feelings.

value.zh: 思良股肱，嘉昔伊呂，搜揚側陋，舉湯代禹；
value.en: He sought worthy limbs of state, praised Yi Yin and Lü Wang, searched humble lanes and raised men like Tang's ministers;
value.literal: Thought good thighs arms—praised former Yi Lü—search raise humble obscure—raise Tang replace Yu;

value.zh: 拔才巖穴，取士蓬戶，唯德是縈，弗拘禰祖。
value.en: he drew talent from mountain caves and brushwood gates, binding office to virtue alone without respect to pedigree.
value.literal: Pull talent cave grottoes—take scholars brushwood doors—only virtue is bound—not constrain Mi Zu.

value.zh: 宅土之表，道義是圖，弗營厥險，六合是虞。
value.en: Beyond the nine provinces he sought righteousness, scorned mere terrain, and watched over the six directions.
value.literal: Dwelling earth's surface—Way righteousness this plan—not fortify those perils—six unions this guard.

value.zh: 齊契共遵，下以純民，恢折規矩，克紹前人。
value.en: All signed the covenant to guide the folk in simplicity, broadened the norms, and carried on the work of past kings.
value.literal: Level tally together obey—below thereby pure people—expand break compass-square—able continue former men.

value.zh: 科條品制，襃貶以因。
value.en: Statutes and ranks framed praise and blame by precedent.
value.literal: Statutes articles grades systems—praise blame thereby follow.

value.zh: 乘殷之輅，行夏之辰。
value.en: He rode Yin-style chariots and kept Xia's calendar.
value.literal: Ride Yin's chariot—practice Xia's calendar.

value.zh: 金根黃屋，翠葆龍鱗，紼冕崇麗，衡紞惟新，尊肅禮容，矚之若神。
value.en: Gold-decked chariot and yellow canopy, kingfisher pennons and dragon scales on regalia; cords and crowns rose in splendor, hatstrings gleamed anew—his solemn ritual awe struck every eye like a god.
value.literal: Gold Root Yellow Canopy—emerald feather dragon scales—cord cap lofty splendid—cross-cord only new—revere solemn ritual bearing—gaze it like spirit.

value.zh: 方牧妙舉，欽於恤民，虎將荷節，鎮彼四鄰；
value.en: Regional governors were wisely chosen and cherished the people; tiger generals bore credentials and pacified the marches;
value.literal: Regional shepherds wonderful selections—revere at relieving people—tiger generals bearing credential—guard those four neighbors;

value.zh: 朱旗所勦，九壤被震，疇克不若？
value.en: Wherever crimson banners swept the nine regions trembled—who could refuse submission?
value.literal: Red flags wherever strike—nine soils struck quake—who can not submit?

value.zh: 孰敢不臣？
value.en: Who dared withhold allegiance?
value.literal: Who dares not minister?

value.zh: 縣旌海表，萬里無塵。
value.en: Banners flew beyond the eastern sea and ten thousand li knew no raider's dust.
value.literal: Suspend banners sea beyond—ten thousand li without dust.

value.zh: 虜備凶徹，鳥殪江岷，權若涸魚，乾腊矯鱗，肅慎納貢，越裳效珍，條支絕域，侍子內賔。
value.en: Liu Bei's host was broken along the rivers; Sun Quan gasped like a fish on dry land; Sushen sent tribute, Yuechang offered jades, even far Tiaozhi sent hostages to court.
value.literal: Captive Bei fierce exhausted—birds destroyed Jiang Min—Quan like dried fish—dried flesh stiff scales—Sushen bring tribute—Yuechang present treasures—Tiaozhi cut-off region—hostage sons inner guests.

value.zh: 德儕先皇，功侔太古。
value.en: His virtue matched the ancient sovereigns; his deeds rivaled high antiquity.
value.literal: Virtue equal Former Emperor—merit match Grand Antiquity.

value.zh: 上靈降瑞，黃初叔祜：河龍洛龜，淩波游下；
value.en: High Heaven sent omens and Huangchu knew felicity: dragons rose from the Yellow River and tortoises from the Luo, breasting the waves;
value.literal: Upper spirits descend auspicious—Huangchu secondary blessing: River Dragon Luo Tortoise—stride waves swim down;

value.zh: 平鈞應繩，神鸞翔舞；
value.en: the measuring cord hung true and divine phoenixes wheeled in dance;
value.literal: Level jun responds cord—divine luan soar dance;

value.zh: 數莢階除，系風扇暑；
value.en: auspicious grain sprouted on the stairs; gentle winds turned aside the summer heat;
value.literal: Repeated pods stair steps—tie wind fan summer;

value.zh: 皓獸素禽，飛走郊野；
value.en: white beasts and bright-plumed birds crossed the suburban preserves;
value.literal: White beasts plain birds—fly run suburban wilds;

value.zh: 神鍾寶鼎，形自舊土；
value.en: spirit bells and bronze tripods took shape from native earth;
value.literal: Divine bell precious tripod—forms from old soil;

value.zh: 雲英甘露，瀸塗被宇；
value.en: sweet nectar washed the dust and bathed the palace roof;
value.literal: Cloud essence sweet dew—moisten mud cover roof;

value.zh: 靈芝冒沼，朱華陰渚。
value.en: magic fungus crowned the ponds and crimson flowers shaded the islets.
value.literal: Numinous fungus cover marsh—red flowers shade islet.

value.zh: 回回凱風，祁祁甘雨，稼穡豐登，我稷我黍。
value.en: Soft southern breezes brought abundant rains; grain stood thick—our wheat and millet flourished.
value.literal: Whirling triumphant wind—vast vast sweet rain—grain crops abundant rising—our millet our glutinous millet.

value.zh: 家佩惠君，戶蒙慈父。
value.en: Every home cherished him as a gracious lord; every door knew him as a kindly father.
value.literal: Households wear gracious lord—doors receive kindly father.

value.zh: 圖致太和，洽德全義。
value.en: He aimed at supreme harmony and mingled virtue with perfect righteousness.
value.literal: Plan reach Grand Harmony—moisten virtue complete righteousness.

value.zh: 將登介山，先皇作儷。
value.en: He prepared to climb Mount Jie as Shun once did, pairing ritual with the founder.
value.literal: About to ascend Jie Mountain—Former Emperor made mate.

value.zh: 鐫石紀勳，兼錄衆瑞，方隆封禪，歸功天地，賔禮百靈，勳命視規，望祭四嶽，燎封奉柴，肅于南郊，宗祀上帝。
value.en: He carved stone to record deeds and gathered every omen; about to mount Feng and Shan he returned merit to Heaven and earth, feasted the hundred spirits, inspected ordinances, sacrificed to the Four Peaks, burned grain offerings at the suburban altar, and honored High God in the ancestral shrine.
value.literal: Carve stone record merit—also record crowd auspicious—about to elevate Feng Shan—return merit Heaven Earth—guest-ritual hundred spirits—merit mandate inspect regulation—gaze sacrifice Four Marchmounts—blaze seal offer firewood—solemn at southern suburb—ancestral sacrifice Supreme Lord.

value.zh: 三牲旣供，夏禘秋甞，元侯佐祭，獻璧奉璋。
value.en: Tripods steamed with three beasts; summer di and autumn chang rites brought chief marquises to assist, presenting disks and libation tablets.
value.literal: Three victims already supplied—summer di autumn taste—chief marquises assist sacrifice—present jade disk offer jade tablet.

value.zh: 鸞輿幽藹，龍旂太常，爰迄太廟，鍾鼓鍠鍠，頌德詠功，八佾鏘鏘。
value.en: Phoenix carriages drifted in gloom; dragon banners flew from the Grand Constant guard; entering the Grand Temple bells and drums thundered while eight rows of dancers praised virtue and rehearsed his deeds.
value.literal: Luan carriage dim mist—dragon pennant Grand Constant—thereupon reach Grand Temple—bells drums clang clang—praise virtue chant merit—eight rows clang clang.

value.zh: 皇祖旣饗，烈考來享，神具醉止，降茲福祥。
value.en: Imperial ancestors received the feast; his father joined in joy—the spirits drank their fill and poured forth fortune.
value.literal: Imperial Grandfather already feast—Fiery Deceased comes enjoy—spirits all drunk stop—descend this blessing auspicious.

value.zh: 天地震蕩，大行康之；
value.en: When heaven and earth convulsed, the late emperor brought peace;
value.literal: Heaven Earth shake surge—Grand Procession rested them;

value.zh: 三辰暗昧，大行光之；
value.en: when sun, moon, and stars grew dim, he lit them anew;
value.literal: Three luminaries dark dim—Grand Procession brightened them;

value.zh: 皇紘絕維，大行綱之；
value.en: when the royal net snapped, he restrung it;
value.literal: Imperial cord cut rope—Grand Procession corded them;

value.zh: 神器莫統，大行當之；
value.en: when the sacred regalia lacked a master, he took it up;
value.literal: Divine vessel none unify—Grand Procession bore it;

value.zh: 禮樂廢弛，大行張之；
value.en: when ritual and music collapsed, he stretched them taut;
value.literal: Rite music abandoned slack—Grand Procession stretched them;

value.zh: 仁義陸沈，大行揚之；
value.en: when humanity and justice sank from sight, he raised them high;
value.literal: Benevolence righteousness sunk land—Grand Procession raised them;

value.zh: 潛龍隱鳳，大行翔之；
value.en: when dragons hid and phoenixes vanished, he gave them flight;
value.literal: Hidden dragon concealed phoenix—Grand Procession soared them;

value.zh: 疏狄遐康，大行匡之。
value.en: when distant Di tribes lacked peace, he set them right.
value.literal: Distant Di far Kang—Grand Procession corrected them.

value.zh: 在位七載，元功仍舉，將永太和，絕迹三五，宜作物師，長爲神主，壽終金石，等筭東父，如何奄忽，摧身后土，俾我棾棾，靡瞻靡顧。
value.en: Seven years on the throne—great deeds piled toward lasting harmony, rivaling the Three Dynasties—fit to be maker of laws and everlasting lord, to live long as bronze stone like Dongfang Shuo—yet suddenly earth swallowed him, leaving us orphaned with nowhere to turn our eyes.
value.literal: On throne seven years—prime merit still raised—about to eternal Grand Harmony—cut traces Three Five—should serve creation teacher—long as spirit lord—life end metal stone—equal reckon Eastern Father—how sudden abruptly—break body rear earth—cause me solitary solitary—none gaze none look.

value.zh: 嗟嗟皇穹，胡寧忍務？
value.en: O mighty Heaven—how could you bear this deed?
value.literal: Alas alas august vault—how indeed endure task?

value.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！
value.en: Alas, the sorrow!
value.literal: Alas how bitter grief!

value.zh: 明監吉凶，體遠存亡，深垂典制，申之嗣皇。
value.en: Clear-eyed toward fortune and fate, he gauged life and death from afar—his ordinances reach deep and instruct the heir.
value.literal: Bright mirror auspicious inauspicious—embody far survival loss—deep suspend canon regulations—extend them heir emperor.

value.zh: 聖上虔奉，是順是將，乃剏玄宇，基爲首陽，擬迹穀林，追堯慕唐，合山同陵，不樹不疆，塗車芻靈，珠玉靡藏。
value.en: The sacred heir reverently follows—raising dark halls on Shouyang as Yao at Grain Grove—honoring Tang without mound rings or jeweled grave goods, only clay hearses and straw figures—no pearls hidden below.
value.literal: Holy superior reverently uphold—this obey this lead—thereupon carve Dark Hall—foundation be Shouyang—trace footprints Grain Grove—pursue Yao admire Tang—join mountains same mound—not trees not borders—clay cart straw spirits—pearls jades none bury.

value.zh: 百神警侍，來賔幽堂，耕禽田獸，望魂之翔。
value.en: Spirits stand vigil as guests enter the shadowed hall; sacrificial oxen and penned beasts await the soaring soul.
value.literal: Hundred spirits alert attend—come guest dark hall—plough birds field beasts—gaze soul's soar.

value.zh: 於是，俟大隧之致功兮，練元辰之淑禎，潛華體於梓宮兮，馮正殿以居靈。
value.en: Now we await the tunnel's completion and choose an auspicious hour—the splendid form rests in the catalpa coffin while his spirit holds court in the main hall.
value.literal: Thereupon—wait great tunnel's achieve merit—practice primal day's fine auspicious—sink splendid body in catalpa palace—by main hall to dwell spirit.

value.zh: 顧望嗣之號咷兮，存臨者之悲聲，悼晏駕之旣修兮，感容車之速征。
value.en: The heir's keening rings out; mourners sob beside him—the curtained hearse departs all too soon.
value.literal: Look hope heir's wail—exist attendant's grief sound—mourn dawn-chariot's already prepared—feel funeral-carriage's swift campaign.

value.zh: 浮飛魂於輕霄兮，就黃墟以滅形，背三光之昭晰兮，歸玄宅之冥冥。
value.en: His soaring soul mounts thin air and sinks into yellow earth—turning from sun, moon, and stars it enters the shadow underworld.
value.literal: Float flying soul in light sky—approach yellow mound to extinguish form—turn back three luminaries' brightness—return dark dwelling's dark-dark.

value.zh: 嗟一往之不反兮，痛閟闥之長扃。
value.en: Alas—there is no returning from that journey; grief bolts the inner gate forever.
value.literal: Alas one-go's not return—pain bolt-door's long bar.

value.zh: 咨遠臣之眇眇兮，成凶諱以怛驚，心孤絕而靡告兮，紛流涕而交頸。
value.en: We distant ministers stand helpless—news of death strikes like thunder; hearts break with none to tell; tears stream until cheeks meet.
value.literal: Sigh distant ministers' tiny tiny—complete ominous taboo thereby sore shock—heart lone cut none tell—many shed tears cross necks.

value.zh: 思恩榮以橫奔兮，閡闕塞之嶢崢，顧衰絰以輕舉兮，迫關防之我嬰。
value.en: Imperial grace bids me gallop thither—yet palace gates rise sheer; I finger mourning hemp yet frontier posts bind me still.
value.literal: Think grace glory to dash cross—block palace pass steep towering—look mourning sash light rise—press barrier ward's me bind.

value.zh: 欲高飛而遙憩兮，憚天網之遠經，遙投骨於山足兮，報恩養於下庭。
value.en: I would soar far to rest yet dread Heaven's wide net—I would cast my bones at the foothill and repay kindness in the lower court.
value.literal: Wish high fly remote rest—fear Heaven-net's far warp—far cast bones at mountain foot—repay grace nurture at lower court.

value.zh: 慨拊心而自悼兮，懼施重而命輕，嗟微驅之是效兮，甘九死而忘生，幾司命之役籍兮，先黃髮而隕零，天蓋高而察卑兮，冀神明之我聽。
value.en: Beating my breast I mourn—duty weighs heavy yet life seems slight; this mean frame would gladly die nine deaths for him—yet fate's ledger strikes gray heads first; Heaven is high yet sees the low—may spirits hear my plea.
value.literal: Sigh strike heart self mourn—fear burden heavy life light—alas slight body's this effect—sweet nine deaths forget life—almost Director of Fate's service register—before yellow hair fall scatter—Heaven cover high examine low—hope spirit-brilliant's me hear.

value.zh: 獨鬱伊而莫愬兮，追顧景而憐形，奏斯文以寫思兮，結翰墨以敷誠。
value.en: Brooding alone with none to speak—I pity this fading shadow and set forth these lines to lay bare devotion.
value.literal: Alone depressed yi none complain—trace look shadow pity form—present this text write thought—tie brush ink spread sincerity.

value.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！」〉
value.en: Alas, the sorrow!"〉"
value.literal: Alas how bitter grief!"〉"

value.zh: 张辽字文远，雁门马邑人也。
value.en: Zhang Liao, whose courtesy name was Wenyuan, came from Mayi in Yanmen commandery.
value.literal: Zhang Liao, courtesy name Wenyuan, was a man of Mayi in Yanmen.

value.zh: 本聂壹之后，以避怨变姓。
value.en: He was descended from Nie Yi but had changed his family name to escape a blood feud.
value.literal: Originally he was a descendant of Nie Yi; to avoid resentment he changed his surname.

value.zh: 少为郡吏。
value.en: As a young man he served as a commandery clerk.
value.literal: In youth he was a clerk of the commandery.

value.zh: 汉末，并州刺史丁原以辽武力过人，召为从事，使将兵诣京都。
value.en: Late in the Han, Ding Yuan, inspector of Bingzhou, impressed by Zhang Liao's exceptional fighting ability, appointed him as an aide-de-camp and sent him at the head of troops to the capital.
value.literal: At the end of Han, the Inspector of Bingzhou, Ding Yuan, because Liao's martial strength surpassed others, summoned him as an aide and ordered him to lead troops to the capital.

value.zh: 何进遣诣河北募兵，得千餘人。
value.en: He Jin sent him north of the river to raise troops, and he returned with over a thousand recruits.
value.literal: He Jin dispatched him to north of the Yellow River to recruit soldiers; he obtained more than a thousand men.

value.zh: 还，进败，以兵属董卓。
value.en: By the time he came back, He Jin had already fallen, and Zhang Liao placed his command under Dong Zhuo.
value.literal: Returning, He Jin had been defeated, and he attached his troops to Dong Zhuo.

value.zh: 卓败，以兵属吕布，迁骑都尉。
value.en: After Dong Zhuo's downfall he joined Lü Bu's forces and was promoted to colonel of cavalry.
value.literal: When Zhuo was defeated, he attached his troops to Lü Bu and was promoted to Colonel of Cavalry.

value.zh: 布为李傕所败，从布东奔徐州，领鲁相，时年二十八。
value.en: When Lü Bu was routed by Li Jue, Zhang Liao followed him east into Xu Province, became administrator of Lu, and was twenty-eight at the time.
value.literal: When Bu was defeated by Li Jue, he followed Bu fleeing east to Xu Province, served as chancellor of Lu, and at that time was twenty-eight years old.

value.zh: 太祖破吕布於下邳，辽将其众降，拜中郎将，赐爵关内侯。
value.en: After Cao Cao took Xiapi and broke Lü Bu, Zhang Liao brought his men over in submission and was named a general of the household and enfeoffed as a secondary marquis at court.
value.literal: The Grand Progenitor defeated Lü Bu at Xiapi; Liao led his multitude in surrender, was appointed General of the Gentlemen of the Household, and was granted the noble rank of secondary marquis within the passes.

value.zh: 数有战功，迁裨将军。
value.en: He won distinction again and again in the field and rose to the rank of major general.
value.literal: Repeatedly he had merit in battle and was promoted to major general.

value.zh: 袁绍破，别遣辽定鲁国诸县。
value.en: Once Yuan Shao had been crushed, Cao Cao detached Zhang Liao to secure every county in the state of Lu.
value.literal: When Yuan Shao was broken, separately he dispatched Liao to pacify the counties of the Lu princedom.

value.zh: 与夏侯渊围昌豨於东海，数月粮尽，议引军还，辽谓渊曰：“数日已来，每行诸围，豨辄属目视辽。
value.en: He joined Xiahou Yuan in besieging Chang Xi in Donghai; when months of campaigning had emptied the granaries and the generals talked of pulling back, Zhang Liao told Xiahou Yuan, Lately, whenever I tour the perimeter, "Chang Xi keeps his gaze fixed on me.
value.literal: Together with Xiahou Yuan he besieged Chang Xi in Donghai; after several months the provisions were exhausted, and they deliberated on withdrawing the army. Liao said to Yuan: For several days now, whenever I have walked the various siege lines, "Xi has always fixed his eyes on Liao.

value.zh: 又其射矢更稀，此必豨计犹豫，故不力战。
value.en: His archery has slackened as well; he must be torn about what to do next, which is why he will not commit to a full fight.
value.literal: Moreover his shooting of arrows has become rarer; this must be because Xi's plans are hesitant, therefore he does not fight hard.

value.zh: 辽欲挑与语，傥可诱也？”
value.en: I would like to draw him into conversation—there may be a way to coax him out."
value.literal: Liao wishes to challenge him to speak; perhaps he can be enticed?"

value.zh: 乃使谓豨曰：“公有命，使辽传之。”
value.en: He then sent a messenger to Chang Xi: Our lord has issued orders, "and he has asked me to relay them to you."
value.literal: Then he sent someone to say to Xi: "The lord has a command; he has ordered Liao to transmit it."

value.zh: 豨果下与辽语，辽为说“太祖神武，方以德怀四方，先附者受大赏”。
value.en: Chang Xi did come down to parley, "and Zhang Liao told him that Cao Cao was a formidable leader who was winning the realm by moral authority and that those who submitted early would be richly rewarded."
value.literal: Xi indeed came down and spoke with Liao, and Liao for him explained that "the Grand Progenitor is divinely martial and is just now by virtue cherishing the four quarters; those who attach first receive great rewards"."

value.zh: 豨乃许降。
value.en: Chang Xi agreed to yield.
value.literal: Xi then promised to surrender.

value.zh: 辽遂单身上三公山，入豨家，拜妻子。
value.en: Zhang Liao then went alone up Mount Sangong, walked into Chang Xi's home, and paid his respects to the man's wife and children.
value.literal: Liao thereupon alone ascended Mount Sangong, entered Xi's house, and bowed to wife and children.

value.zh: 豨欢喜，随诣太祖。
value.en: Delighted, Chang Xi accompanied him to Cao Cao's headquarters.
value.literal: Xi was pleased and followed to go to the Grand Progenitor.

value.zh: 太祖遣豨还，责辽曰：“此非大将法也。”
value.en: Cao Cao sent Chang Xi back to his post and rebuked Zhang Liao: "That is not how a senior commander should behave."
value.literal: The Grand Progenitor sent Xi back and reproached Liao, saying: "This is not the method of a great general."

value.zh: 辽谢曰：“以明公威信著於四海，辽奉圣旨，豨必不敢害故也。”
value.en: Zhang Liao bowed and replied, I knew your authority reaches every corner of the land and that I bore your written order, "so Chang Xi would never have dared harm me."
value.literal: Liao apologized, saying: Because the enlightened lord's prestige and trust are manifest throughout the four seas, and Liao carried out the sage command, "Xi certainly did not dare to harm; that is the reason."

value.zh: 从讨袁谭、袁尚於黎阳，有功，行中坚将军。
value.en: He took part in the campaign against Yuan Tan and Yuan Shang at Liyang, distinguished himself, and was given acting rank as general of the central corps.
value.literal: He followed in attacking Yuan Tan and Yuan Shang at Liyang, had merit, and acted as general of the central solid.

value.zh: 从攻尚於鄴，尚坚守不下。
value.en: He joined the assault on Ye, where Yuan Shang held the walls and could not be dislodged.
value.literal: He followed in attacking Shang at Ye; Shang firmly defended and was not taken.

value.zh: 太祖还许，使辽与乐进拔阴安，徙其民河南。
value.en: When Cao Cao withdrew to Xu, he sent Zhang Liao and Yue Jin to take Yin'an and resettle its population south of the river.
value.literal: The Grand Progenitor returned to Xu and ordered Liao together with Yue Jin to seize Yin'an and move its people south of the Yellow River.

value.zh: 复从攻鄴，鄴破，辽别徇赵国、常山，招降缘山诸贼及黑山孙轻等。
value.en: He returned for the siege of Ye, and after the city fell he swept Zhao and Changshan on a separate line, bringing the mountain outlaws and Black Mountain leaders such as Sun Qing to terms.
value.literal: Again he followed in attacking Ye; when Ye was broken, Liao separately campaigned through Zhao and Changshan, summoning to surrender the various bandits along the mountains and Sun Qing of the Black Mountain band, and others.

value.zh: 从攻袁谭，谭破，别将徇海滨，破辽东贼柳毅等。
value.en: He fought in the final campaign against Yuan Tan, then led a detached column along the coast and smashed coastal raiders from Liaodong led by Liu Yi.
value.literal: He followed in attacking Yuan Tan; when Tan was broken, as a separate general he campaigned along the seacoast and defeated the Liaodong bandits Liu Yi and others.

value.zh: 还鄴，太祖自出迎辽，引共载，以辽为荡寇将军。
value.en: Back in Ye, Cao Cao rode out in person to greet him, had him share his carriage, and named him general who sweeps away bandits.
value.literal: Returning to Ye, the Grand Progenitor himself came out to welcome Liao, led him to ride together in the same carriage, and appointed Liao general who sweeps away bandits.

value.zh: 复别击荆州，定江夏诸县，还屯临颍，封都亭侯。
value.en: He campaigned again into Jingzhou, secured the Jiangxia counties, took station at Linying on his return, and received a village marquisate at the capital.
value.literal: Again separately he struck Jing Province, pacified the counties of Jiangxia, returned and garrisoned Linying, and was enfeoffed as marquis of the metropolitan village.

value.zh: 从征袁尚於柳城，卒与虏遇，辽劝太祖战，气甚奋，太祖壮之，自以所持麾授辽。
value.en: During the expedition against Yuan Shang at Liucheng they ran straight into the nomad host; Zhang Liao pressed Cao Cao to give battle, and his fervor so impressed Cao Cao that he passed him his own command banner.
value.literal: He followed in campaigning against Yuan Shang at Liucheng; suddenly they encountered the barbarians. Liao urged the Grand Progenitor to fight; his spirit was very aroused; the Grand Progenitor thought him brave and personally handed the banner he held to Liao.

value.zh: 遂击，大破之，斩单于蹋顿。
value.en: They attacked at once, shattered the enemy, and killed the chanyu Tadun.
value.literal: Thereupon they attacked, greatly defeated them, and beheaded the Shanyu Tadun.

value.zh: 〈《傅子》曰：太祖将征柳城，辽谏曰：“夫许，天子之会也。
value.en: 〈The Fu zi records that when Cao Cao was preparing the Liucheng expedition, Zhang Liao urged him to reconsider: "Xu is where the emperor resides.
value.literal: 〈The Fu zi says: When the Grand Progenitor was about to campaign to Liucheng, Liao remonstrated, saying: "Now Xu is the assembly place of the Son of Heaven.

value.zh: 今天子在许，公远北征，若刘表遣刘备袭许，据之以号令四方，公之势去矣。”
value.en: The sovereign is at Xu while you march deep into the north; if Liu Biao sent Liu Bei to strike the capital, seize it, and issue orders from there, your position would collapse."
value.literal: Now the Son of Heaven is at Xu; the lord campaigns far to the north; if Liu Biao dispatches Liu Bei to raid Xu, occupies it, and by it issues commands to the four quarters, the lord's situation will be gone."

value.zh: 太祖策表必不能任备，遂行也。〉
value.en: Cao Cao judged that Liu Biao would never give Liu Bei real authority, and went ahead with the campaign anyway.
value.literal: The Grand Progenitor calculated that Biao certainly could not employ Bei, and thereupon proceeded.

value.zh: 诸葛亮复出祁山，诏郃督诸将西至略阳，亮还保祁山，郃追至木门，与亮军交战，飞矢中郃右膝，薨，
value.en: When Zhuge Liang again drove toward Qishan, an edict sent Zhang He west to Lueyang; as Zhuge Liang fell back on Qishan, Zhang He pursued to Mumen, where in the fighting an arrow struck his right knee and he died,
value.literal: When Zhuge Liang again came out to Qishan, an edict ordered He to supervise the various generals west to Lueyang; Liang returned to protect Qishan; He pursued to Mumen, joined battle with Liang's army, a flying arrow struck He's right knee, and he died,

value.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：亮军退，司马宣王使郃追之，郃曰：“军法，围城必开出路，归军勿追。”
value.en: 〈The Wei lüe records that when Zhuge Liang withdrew, Sima Yi ordered Zhang He to pursue; Zhang He said, "The art of war says to leave a way out of a siege and never to chase a retreating host."
value.literal: 〈The Wei lüe says: When Liang's army withdrew, Sima Xuanwang ordered He to pursue them; He said: By military law, "when besieging a city one must open an escape route; do not pursue a withdrawing army."

value.zh: 宣王不听。
value.en: Sima Yi would not hear of it.
value.literal: Xuanwang did not listen.

value.zh: 郃不得已，遂进。
value.en: Zhang He had no choice but to advance.
value.literal: He had no choice and thereupon advanced.

value.zh: 蜀军乘高布伏，弓弩乱发，矢中郃髀。〉
value.en: The Shu troops held the heights in ambush and raked him with bolts; an arrow struck him in the thigh.〉
value.literal: The Shu army rode the heights and laid ambush; crossbows shot wildly; an arrow struck He's thigh.〉

value.zh: 谥曰壮侯。
value.en: He was posthumously titled Marquis Zhuang, "the Stalwart."
value.literal: His posthumous title was Marquis Zhuang.

value.zh: 子雄嗣。
value.en: His son Zhang Xiong inherited the title.
value.literal: The son Xiong inherited.

value.zh: 郃前后征伐有功，明帝分郃户，封郃四子列侯。
value.en: For his long record of service Emperor Ming divided his fief and enfeoffed four of Zhang He's sons as full marquises.
value.literal: He before and after campaigning had merit; Emperor Ming divided He's households and enfeoffed He's four sons as full marquises.

value.zh: 赐小子爵关内侯。
value.en: His youngest son received a secondary marquisate at court.
value.literal: His youngest son was granted the noble rank of secondary marquis within the passes.

value.zh: 後主 劉禪
value.en: The Later Lord: Liu Shan.
value.literal: The Later Lord, Liu Shan.

value.zh: 八年秋，魏使司馬懿由西城，張郺由子午，曹真由斜谷，
value.en: In the autumn of 230 Wei launched a three-pronged move on Hanzhong: Sima Yi through Xicheng, Zhang He through the Ziwu defile, and Cao Zhen up the Xie Valley,
value.literal: In the autumn of the eighth year, Wei sent Sima Yi by Xicheng, Zhang He by Ziwu, and Cao Zhen by Xie Valley,

value.zh: 〈斜，余奢反。〉
value.en: 〈Commentary gloss: the graph xie is read with the yu-she fanqie.〉
value.literal: 〈Xie: read with the fanqie initial yu and final she.〉

value.zh: 欲攻漢中。
value.en: intending to overrun Hanzhong.
value.literal: intending to attack Hanzhong.

value.zh: 丞相亮待之於城固、赤坂，大雨道絕，真等皆還。
value.en: Zhuge Liang blocked them at Chenggu and Chipo; torrential rains washed out the roads, and Cao Zhen's columns had to turn back.
value.literal: Chancellor Liang awaited them at Chenggu and Chipo; great rain cut off the roads, and Zhen and the others all returned.

value.zh: 是歲，魏延破魏雍州剌史郭淮於陽溪。
value.en: The same year Wei Yan routed Yongzhou inspector Guo Huai for Wei at Yangxi.
value.literal: That year, Wei Yan defeated Wei's Inspector of Yongzhou Guo Huai at Yangxi.

value.zh: 徙魯王永為甘陵王，梁王理為安平王，皆以魯、梁在吳分界故也。
value.en: Prince Yong of Lu was redesignated prince of Ganling and Prince Li of Liang became prince of Pingan, since Lu and Liang lay in territory allotted to Wu.
value.literal: The Prince of Lu Yong was moved to be Prince of Ganling, and the Prince of Liang Li was moved to be Prince of Pingan—both because Lu and Liang lay on Wu's side of the partition.

value.zh: 九年春二月，亮復出軍圍祁山，始以木牛運。
value.en: In the second month of 231 Zhuge Liang marched on Qishan again, this time supplying the army with his wooden-ox carts.
value.literal: In the spring, second month, of the ninth year, Liang again went out with the army and besieged Qishan, for the first time using the wooden ox to transport.

value.zh: 魏司馬懿、張郺救祁山。
value.en: Sima Yi and Zhang He of Wei raced to lift the siege at Qishan.
value.literal: Wei's Sima Yi and Zhang He relieved Qishan.

value.zh: 夏六月，亮糧盡退軍，郺追至青封，與亮交戰，被箭死。
value.en: By the sixth month Zhuge Liang had exhausted his grain and fell back; Zhang He pressed him to Qingfeng, joined battle, and was killed by an arrow.
value.literal: In the summer, sixth month, when Liang's provisions were exhausted he withdrew the army; He pursued to Qingfeng, fought with Liang, and was hit by an arrow and died.

value.zh: 秋八月，都護李嚴廢徙梓潼郡。
value.en: That August Li Yan was stripped of office and exiled to Zitong.
value.literal: In the autumn, eighth month, Chief Controller Li Yan was dismissed and banished to Zitong commandery.

value.zh: 〈《漢晉春秋》曰：冬十月，江陽至江州有鳥從江南飛渡江北，不能達，墮水死者以千數。〉
value.en: 〈The Han–Jin Annals of Spring and Autumn record that in the tenth month flocks tried to fly from the south bank of the Yangzi toward Jiangzhou; thousands dropped into the river and drowned.〉
value.literal: 〈The Han Jin chunqiu states: In the winter, tenth month, from Jiangyang to Jiangzhou there were birds flying from south of the Yangzi to cross north of the Yangzi; unable to reach, they fell into the water and died by the thousands.〉

value.zh: 劉封者，本羅侯寇氏之子，長沙劉氏之甥也。
value.en: Liu Feng was born to the Kou house of Marquis Luo and was the nephew of the Liu clan of Changsha.
value.literal: Liu Feng was originally the son of Marquis Luo of the Kou clan and the nephew of the Liu family of Changsha.

value.zh: 先主至荊州，以未有繼嗣，養封為子。
value.en: When Liu Bei reached Jing Province he still had no heir, so he adopted Liu Feng as his son.
value.literal: When the Former Lord arrived in Jing Province, because he had yet no heir, he adopted Feng as a son.

value.zh: 及先主入蜀，自葭萌還攻劉璋，時封年二十馀，有武藝，氣力過人，將兵俱與諸葛亮、張飛等溯流西上，所在戰克。
value.en: When Liu Bei marched into Shu from Jiameng against Liu Zhang, Liu Feng was already in his twenties—strong, skilled in arms, and bold enough to lead men beside Zhuge Liang and Zhang Fei upriver into the west, victorious at every turn.
value.literal: When the Former Lord entered Shu and turned back from Jiameng to attack Liu Zhang, at that time Feng was over twenty, had martial skill, and strength surpassing others; he led troops together with Zhuge Liang, Zhang Fei, and others up the river westward, winning victory wherever they fought.

value.zh: 益州既定，以封為副軍中郎將。
value.en: Once Yi Province was secured, Liu Feng became a general of the household serving as deputy to the army.
value.literal: After Yi Province was settled, Feng was appointed General of the Household, Deputy to the Army.

value.zh: 九年春，亮軍祁山，平催督運事。
value.en: In the spring of 231 Zhuge Liang was at Qishan; Li Ping oversaw supply runs.
value.literal: In the spring of the ninth year, Liang’s army was at Qishan; Ping urged and supervised transport affairs.

value.zh: 秋夏之際，值天霖雨，運糧不繼，平遣參軍狐忠、督軍成籓喻指，呼亮來還；
value.en: Autumn rains cut the supply line; Li Ping sent Hu Zhong and Cheng Fan with orders for Zhuge Liang to pull back;
value.literal: Between autumn and summer it happened that Heaven sent continuous rain; grain transport did not continue; Ping sent staff adviser Hu Zhong and supervisor Cheng Fan with instructions, summoning Liang to return;

value.zh: 亮承以退軍。
value.en: Zhuge Liang obeyed and withdrew.
value.literal: Liang accepted and withdrew the army.

value.zh: 平聞軍退，乃更陽驚，說「軍糧饒足，何以便歸」！
value.en: Then Li Ping feigned shock: “We have plenty of grain—why retreat?”
value.literal: When Ping heard the army had withdrawn, then feigned surprise, saying “Army grain is abundant—why return so soon!”

value.zh: 欲以解己不辦之責，顯亮不進之愆也。
value.en: He meant to blame Zhuge Liang for timidity and cover his own logistics failure.
value.literal: He wished thereby to excuse his own failure to deliver and display Liang’s fault for not advancing.

value.zh: 又表後主，說「軍偽退，欲以誘賊與戰」。
value.en: He also memorialized the Later Lord, saying “The army feigned retreat, wishing thereby to lure the bandits to battle.”
value.literal: He also memorialized the Later Lord, saying “The army feigned retreat, wishing thereby to lure the bandits to battle.”

value.zh: 亮具出其前後手筆書疏本末，平違錯章灼。
value.en: Zhuge Liang produced their correspondence; Li Ping’s lies stood exposed.
value.literal: Liang produced in full his earlier and later handwritten letters and memorials’ beginning and end—Ping’s violation and error were manifestly clear.

value.zh: 平辭窮情竭，首謝罪負。
value.en: Cornered, Li Ping confessed.
value.literal: Ping’s words were exhausted and feeling spent; he bowed and confessed guilt.

value.zh: 於是亮表平曰：「自先帝崩後，平所在治家，尚為小惠，安身求名，無憂國之事。
value.en: Zhuge Liang wrote: “Since the late emperor died Li Ping has tended his private affairs, traded petty favours for reputation, and ignored the state.
value.literal: Thereupon Liang memorialized Ping, saying: “Since the Former Lord’s passing, wherever Ping has been he has managed his household, still doing petty kindnesses, securing himself and seeking fame—there are no affairs of worrying for the state.

value.zh: 臣當北出，欲得平兵以鎮漢中，平窮難縱橫，無有來意，而求以五郡為巴州刺史。
value.en: When I marched north I asked him to hold Hanzhong; he stalled and demanded to be inspector over five commanderies as Ba province.
value.literal: When your servant should go north, I wished to obtain Ping’s troops to garrison Hanzhong; Ping raised difficulties in every direction and had no intent to come, yet sought to make five commanderies into Inspector of Ba Province.

value.zh: 去年臣欲西征，欲令平主督漢中，平說司馬懿等開府闢召。
value.en: Last year I meant to leave him Hanzhong; he answered that Sima Yi was recruiting worthies.
value.literal: Last year your servant wished to campaign west and wished to order Ping to take charge of Hanzhong; Ping spoke of Sima Yi and others opening offices and summoning recruits.

value.zh: 臣知平鄙情，欲因行之際偪臣取利也，是以表平子豐督主江州，隆崇其遇，以取一時之務。
value.en: I knew he meant to profit from my absence, so I honoured his son Li Feng in Jiangzhou to keep him quiet.
value.literal: Your servant knew Ping’s base intent—wishing on the march’s occasion to coerce your servant for profit; therefore your servant memorialized Ping’s son Feng to supervise Jiangzhou, greatly honouring his treatment, to settle the moment’s tasks.

value.zh: 平至之日，都委諸事，群臣上下皆怪臣待平之厚也。
value.en: When he arrived I gave him full trust—the court marvelled at my generosity.
value.literal: When Ping arrived, all affairs were entrusted to him; host of ministers above and below all marvelled at how thickly your servant treated Ping.

value.zh: 正以大事未定，漢室傾危，伐平之短，莫若褒之。
value.en: The realm still hung in the balance—praise worked better than blame.
value.literal: Just because the great task was not settled and the Han house leaned toward peril—to attack Ping’s shortcomings was not as good as praising him.

value.zh: 然謂平情在於榮利而已，不意平心顛倒乃爾。
value.en: I thought he only cranked rank and wealth—I never dreamed he would sink this low.
value.literal: Yet your servant thought Ping’s intent lay only in glory and profit—did not expect Ping’s heart to be upside-down thus.

value.zh: 若事稽留，將致禍敗，是臣不敏，言多增咎。」
value.en: If delay ruins the campaign, the fault is mine for trusting him too long.”
value.literal: If affairs drag and delay, will bring calamity and defeat—this is your servant’s dullness; words add more fault.”

value.zh: 〈亮公文上尚書曰：「平為大臣，受恩過量，不思忠報，橫造無端，危恥不辦，迷罔上下，論獄棄科，導人為奸，
value.en: 〈Zhuge Liang’s official document to the Ministry says: “As a great minister, Li Ping received favor beyond measure, yet he gave no thought to repaying it with loyalty. He recklessly invented groundless claims, failed to deal with danger and disgrace, deceived superiors and subordinates alike, discarded legal standards in judging cases, and led others into wrongdoing,
value.literal: 〈Liang’s official document to the Ministry says: “Ping as great minister received favour beyond measure; did not think to repay with loyalty; recklessly created without cause; peril and shame unmet; deluded above and below; argued lawsuits abandoning statute; led men to wickedness,

value.zh: （狹情）
value.en: 〈variant: narrow sentiment〉
value.literal: (narrow feeling)

value.zh: 情狹志狂，若無天地。
value.en: petty, arrogant, as though heaven and earth did not exist.
value.literal: narrow of temper ambition mad, as if without Heaven and Earth.

value.zh: 自度姦露，嫌心遂生，聞軍臨至，西鄉託疾還沮、漳，軍臨至沮，復還江陽，平參軍狐忠勤諫乃止。
value.en: Sensing exposure he fled west toward Ju and Zhang, doubled back to Jiangyang, until his aide Hu Zhong stopped him.
value.literal: Estimating himself exposed in treachery, suspicious heart then arose; hearing the army drew near, westward feigned illness returning to Ju and Zhang; when army drew near Ju, returned again to Jiangyang—Ping’s staff adviser Hu Zhong earnestly remonstrated and only then stopped.

value.zh: 今篡賊未滅，社稷多難，國事惟和，可以克捷，不可苞含，以危大業。
value.en: Wei still stands; national crisis demands unity—we cannot shelter traitors and risk the realm.
value.literal: Now the usurping bandit is not yet destroyed; altars and grain face many hardships—state affairs rely on harmony to achieve victory; cannot wrap and contain to endanger the great enterprise.

value.zh: 輒與行中軍師車騎將軍都鄉侯臣劉琰，使持節前軍師征西大將軍領涼州刺史南鄭侯臣魏延、前將軍都亭侯臣袁綝、左將軍領荊州刺史高陽鄉侯臣吳壹、督前部右將軍玄鄉侯臣高翔、督後部後將軍安樂亭侯臣吳班、領長史綏軍將軍臣楊儀、督左部行中監軍揚武將軍臣鄧芝、行前監軍征南將軍臣劉巴、行中護軍偏將軍臣費禕、行前護軍偏將軍漢成亭侯臣許允、行左護軍篤信中郎將臣丁咸、行右護軍偏將軍臣劉敏、行護軍征南將軍當陽亭侯臣姜維、行中典軍討虜將軍臣上官雝、行中參軍昭武中郎將臣胡濟、行參軍建義將軍臣閻晏、行參軍偏將軍臣爨習、行參軍裨將軍臣杜義、行參軍武略中郎將臣杜祺、行參軍綏戎都尉盛勃、領從事中郎武略中郎將臣樊岐等議，輒解平任，免官祿、節傳、印綬、符策，削其爵土。」〉
value.en: I therefore deliberated with Liu Yan, acting Central Army Adviser, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Marquis of Duxiang; Wei Yan, bearer of the tally, Former Army Adviser, Grand General Who Conquers the West, acting Inspector of Liang Province, and Marquis of Nanzheng; Yuan Lin, Former General and Marquis of Duting; Wu Yi, General of the Left, acting Inspector of Jing Province, and Marquis of Gaoyangxiang; Gao Xiang, commander of the front division, General of the Right, and Marquis of Xuanxiang; Wu Ban, commander of the rear division, General of the Rear, and Marquis of Anleting; Yang Yi, chief clerk and General Who Pacifies the Army; Deng Zhi, commander of the left division, acting Central Army Supervisor, and General Who Displays Might; Liu Ba, acting front supervisor and General Who Conquers the South; Fei Yi, acting Central Protector of the Army and lieutenant general; Xu Yun, acting Front Protector of the Army, lieutenant general, and Marquis of Hanchengting; Ding Xian, acting Left Protector of the Army and Gentleman General of Earnest Trust; Liu Min, acting Right Protector of the Army and lieutenant general; Jiang Wei, acting Protector of the Army, General Who Conquers the South, and Marquis of Dangyangting; Shangguan Yong, acting Central Army Director and General Who Punishes Caitiffs; Hu Ji, acting Central Staff Adviser and Gentleman General of Brilliant Might; Yan Yan, acting Staff Adviser and General Who Establishes Righteousness; Cuan Xi, acting Staff Adviser and lieutenant general; Du Yi, acting Staff Adviser and assistant general; Du Qi, acting Staff Adviser and Gentleman General of Martial Strategy; Sheng Bo, acting Staff Adviser and Commandant Who Pacifies the Rong; Fan Qi, acting Attendant Clerk and Gentleman General of Martial Strategy; and the others. We have removed Li Ping from his post, stripped him of office, salary, tally, travel credential, seals, ribbons, patents, and warrants, and cut away his noble lands.”〉
value.literal: Thereupon together with Acting Army Adviser General of Chariots and Cavalry Marquis of Dou Village Liu Yan, Bearer of Insignia Former Army Adviser Grand General Who Conquers the West Concurrent Inspector of Liang Province Marquis of Nan Zheng Wei Yan, Former General Marquis of Du Village Yuan Yi, Left General Concurrent Inspector of Jing Province Marquis of Gaoyang Village Wu Yi, Supervisor of Front Section General of the Right Marquis of Xuan Village Gao Xiang, Supervisor of Rear Section General of the Rear Marquis of Anle Village Wu Ban, Chief Clerk General Who Pacifies the Army Yang Yi, Supervisor of Left Section Acting Central Army Supervisor General Who Displays Might Deng Zhi, Acting Former Supervisor General Who Conquers the South Liu Ba, Acting Central Protector of the Army Lieutenant General Fei Yi, Acting Former Protector of the Army Lieutenant General Marquis of Hancheng Village Xu Yun, Acting Left Protector of the Army Faithful General of the Household Ding Xian, Acting Right Protector of the Army Lieutenant General Liu Min, Acting Protector of the Army General Who Conquers the South Marquis of Dangyang Village Jiang Wei, Acting Central Army Director General Who Punishes Barbarians Shangguan Yong, Acting Central Staff Adviser General of Brilliant Might Hu Ji, Acting Staff Adviser General Who Establishes Righteousness Yan Yan, Acting Staff Adviser Lieutenant General Cuan Xi, Acting Staff Adviser General of the Household Du Yi, Acting Staff Adviser General of Martial Stratagem Du Qi, Acting Staff Adviser Pacification Commandant of the Rong Sheng Bo, Concurrent Attendant Clerk General of Martial Stratagem Fan Qi, and others deliberated—thereupon removed Ping from office, stripped official salary, insignia courier, seals and ribbons, tallies and patents, and cut his noble lands.”〉

value.zh: 乃廢平為民，徙梓潼郡。
value.en: Li Ping was reduced to commoner status and exiled to Zitong.
value.literal: Thereupon Ping was reduced to commoner and moved to Zitong Commandery.

value.zh: 〈諸葛亮又與平子豐教曰：「吾與君父子戮力以獎漢室，此神明所聞，非但人知之也。
value.en: 〈Zhuge Liang wrote Li Feng: “Your father and I laboured for Han—Heaven knows it.
value.literal: 〈Zhuge Liang again instructed Ping’s son Feng, saying: “I with you, father and son, joined strength to aid the Han house—this the spirits have heard, not only men know it.

value.zh: 表都護典漢中，委君於東關者，不與人議也。
value.en: I meant to give him Hanzhong and you the eastern gate without debate.
value.literal: Memorializing the Director of Retainers to govern Hanzhong, entrusting you at the eastern pass—not consulted with others.

value.zh: 謂至心感動，終始可保，何圖中乖乎！
value.en: I trusted hearts would stay true—who foresaw this breach?
value.literal: I thought utmost hearts would move each other—beginning and end could be kept—who plotted mid-course betrayal!

value.zh: 昔楚卿屢絀，亦乃克復，思道則福，應自然之數也。
value.en: Great ministers fall and rise again—virtue brings restoration.
value.literal: Formerly Chu ministers were repeatedly dismissed—yet could recover; pondering the Way brings blessing—it answers nature’s reckoning.

value.zh: 原寬慰都護，勤追前闕。
value.en: Comfort your father and help him atone.
value.literal: I beg you comfort the Director of Retainers and diligently pursue remedying former faults.

value.zh: 今雖解任，形業失故，奴婢賓客百數十人，君以中郎參軍居府，方之氣類，猶為上家。
value.en: Though dismissed he keeps scores of servants; you remain an attendant at headquarters—still a great house.
value.literal: Now although office is removed, form and estate lose their old state—yet slaves, maids, and guests number over a hundred; you as Gentleman of the Household staff adviser dwell at headquarters—compared to peers of your kind, still count as upper households.

value.zh: 若都護思負一意，君與公琰推心從事者，否可複通，逝可複還也。
value.en: If he owns his fault and you and Jiang Wan work in good faith, doors can reopen.
value.literal: If the Director of Retainers ponders fault with single mind, you and Gongyan push hearts and serve affairs—blocked can again open; departed can again return.

value.zh: 詳思斯戒，明吾用心，臨書長嘆，涕泣而已。」〉
value.en: Read this and know my heart—I sign in tears.”〉"
value.literal: Think carefully on this warning; clarify my intent—facing the letter I sigh long; tears only.”〉"

value.zh: 霍峻字仲邈，南郡枝江人也。
value.en: Huo Jun, styled Zhongmiao, came from Zhijiang in Nan Commandery.
value.literal: Huo Jun, courtesy name Zhongmiao, was a man of Zhijiang in Nan Commandery.

value.zh: 兄篤於鄉里合部曲數百人，篤卒，荊州牧劉表令峻攝其眾。
value.en: His older brother Huo Du had raised a few hundred local followers; after Du died, Jing governor Liu Biao put Jun in charge of that band.
value.literal: His elder brother Huo Du in the countryside assembled several hundred retainers in a private corps; when Du died, the Governor of Jing Province, Liu Biao, ordered Jun to take command of his troops.

value.zh: 表卒，峻率眾歸先主，先主以峻為中郎將。
value.en: After Liu Biao’s death, Jun brought his men to Liu Bei, who made him a general of the household.
value.literal: When Liu Biao died, Jun led the troops to submit to the First Sovereign, who appointed Jun General of the Gentlemen of the Household.

value.zh: 先主自葭萌南還襲劉璋，留峻守葭萌城。
value.en: Liu Bei marched south from Jiameng to attack Liu Zhang and left Huo Jun to hold the fortress there.
value.literal: The First Sovereign returned south from Jiameng to strike Liu Zhang, leaving Jun to defend Jiameng city.

value.zh: 張魯遣將楊帛誘峻，求共守城，峻曰：「小人頭可得，城不可得。」
value.en: Zhang Lu’s officer Yang Bo tried to win him over for a joint defense, but Huo Jun replied, "You may have my head; you will not have this city."
value.literal: Zhang Lu sent the general Yang Bo to entice Jun, seeking to defend the city together; Jun said, "This petty man's head may be taken, but the city cannot be taken."

value.zh: 帛乃退去。
value.en: Yang Bo withdrew his force.
value.literal: Bo thereupon withdrew.

value.zh: 後璋將扶禁、向存等帥萬餘人由閬水上，攻圍攻峻，且一年，不能下。
value.en: Liu Zhang’s generals Fu Jin and Xiang Cun then brought over ten thousand men up the Lang River and besieged the town for the better part of a year without breaking it.
value.literal: Later Zhang's generals Fu Jin, Xiang Cun, and others led more than ten thousand men up the Lang River, attacked, besieged, and assaulted Jun for nearly a year but could not take him.

value.zh: 峻城中兵才數百人，伺其怠隙，選精銳出擊，大破之，即斬存首。
value.en: Huo Jun had only a few hundred defenders. When he saw an opening, he sent picked troops out in a sortie, routed the besiegers, and took Xiang Cun’s head.
value.literal: Jun had only several hundred soldiers in the city; watching for their slackness and gaps, he selected crack troops, sallied out, struck them a great defeat, and beheaded Cun on the spot.

value.zh: 先主定蜀，嘉峻之功，乃分廣漢為梓潼郡，以峻為梓潼太守、裨將軍。
value.en: Once Liu Bei had secured Shu, he singled out Huo Jun’s exploit, carved Zitong commandery out of Guanghan, and named him its governor with the rank of major general.
value.literal: The First Sovereign settled Shu, praised Jun's merit, thereupon divided Guanghan to make Zitong Commandery, and appointed Jun Administrator of Zitong and Major General.

value.zh: 在官三年，年四十卒，還葬成都。
value.en: He served three years in post, died at forty, and was brought home for burial in Chengdu.
value.literal: In office three years, at age forty he died; he was returned for burial at Chengdu.

value.zh: 先主甚悼惜，乃詔諸葛亮曰：「峻既佳士，加有功於國，欲行爵。」
value.en: The First Sovereign mourned him deeply and issued an edict to Zhuge Liang: "Jun was an excellent man and, moreover, had rendered merit to the state. I wish to grant him rank."
value.literal: The First Sovereign greatly mourned and pitied him, then issued an edict to Zhuge Liang saying, "Jun is already an excellent gentleman, moreover having merit for the state; I wish to carry out enfeoffment."

value.zh: 遂親率群僚臨會弔祭，因留宿墓上，當時榮之。
value.en: He then led the full court to the funeral, stayed the night by the grave, and contemporaries counted it the highest honor.
value.literal: Thereupon he personally led the host of officials to attend the assembly, mourn, and sacrifice, and on that account lodged overnight on the tomb; at the time they deemed it glorious.

value.zh: 建興三年，隨諸葛亮南行，歸至漢陽縣，降人李鴻來詣亮，亮見鴻，時蔣琬與詩在坐。
value.en: In 225, returning with Zhuge Liang from the southern campaign, they reached Hanyang county, where the defector Li Hong came to see Zhuge Liang; Jiang Wan and Fei Shi were present.
value.literal: In the third year of Jianxing, he followed Zhuge Liang south; returning reached Hanyang county; surrendered man Li Hong came to visit Liang; Liang saw Hong; at the time Jiang Wan and Shi were seated.

value.zh: 鴻曰：「聞過孟達許，適見王沖從南來，言往者達之去就，明公切齒，欲誅達妻子，賴先主不聽言。
value.en: Li Hong said, "I heard this while passing through Meng Da's area. I happened to meet Wang Chong coming from the south, and he said that when Da changed allegiance in the past, Your Excellency ground your teeth and wanted to execute Da's wife and children, but fortunately the First Sovereign would not listen to the proposal.
value.literal: Hong said, "I heard passing Meng Da's place, just then saw Wang Chong coming from the south, speaking of former times Da's going and coming, the enlightened lord gnashed teeth, wished to execute Da's wife and children, relied on the First Sovereign not listening to the words.

value.zh: 達曰：『諸葛亮見顧有本末，終不爾也。』
value.en: Meng Da had replied that Zhuge Liang’s goodwill had always been consistent and he would never do such a thing.
value.literal: Da said, 'Zhuge Liang's regard has beginning and end; in the end will not be thus.

value.zh: 盡不信沖言，委仰明公，無復已已。」
value.en: He wholly did not believe Chong's words, entrusted and looked up to the enlightened lord, no more end."
value.literal: He wholly did not believe Chong's words, entrusted and looked up to the enlightened lord, no more end."

value.zh: 亮謂琬、詩曰：「還都當有書與子度相聞。」
value.en: Liang said to Wan and Shi, "When returning to the capital there ought to be a letter to exchange news with Zidu."
value.literal: Liang said to Wan and Shi, "When returning to the capital there ought to be a letter to exchange news with Zidu."

value.zh: 詩進曰：「孟達小子，昔事振威不忠，後又背叛先主，反覆之人，何足與書邪！」
value.en: Fei Shi said, "Meng Da is a petty man. He was disloyal when he formerly served the General Who Inspires Awe, and later he betrayed the First Sovereign as well. A man so changeable is not worth exchanging letters with!"
value.literal: Shi advanced saying, "Meng Da the petty fellow, formerly served General Who Strikes Terror disloyally, afterward again betrayed the First Sovereign—a man of back and forth—what worth to exchange letters!"

value.zh: 亮默然不答。
value.en: Zhuge Liang said nothing.
value.literal: Liang was silent and did not answer.

value.zh: 亮欲誘達以為外援，竟與達書曰：「往年南征，歲
value.en: Zhuge Liang wished to draw Meng Da in as an outside ally and ultimately wrote him a letter: "In former years, during the southern campaign, before the year
value.literal: Liang wished to entice Da to be an external aid; in the end wrote Da a letter saying, "In former years on the southern campaign, before the year

value.zh: （未及）
value.en: (before the year had ended)
value.literal: (not yet reached)

value.zh: [末及]還，適與李鴻會於漢陽，承知消息，慨然永歎，以存足下平素之志，豈徒空托名榮，貴為乘離乎！
value.en: had closed I was still on the road; I met Li Hong at Hanyang and learned your mind. I sighed long for the loyalty you have always shown—surely you do not seek empty glory while we remain apart!
value.literal: had ended I returned, just then met Li Hong at Hanyang, received and knew your message, sighed long with feeling—thereby to preserve your foot's constant purpose—how merely empty entrusting name and glory, prized as riding estrangement!

value.zh: 嗚呼孟子，斯實劉封侵陵足下，以傷先主待士之義。
value.en: Alas, Meng Da—it was Liu Feng’s bullying that wronged you and violated the late emperor’s duty to his men.
value.literal: Alas, Mengzi, this truly was Liu Feng encroaching and bullying you, thereby harming the First Sovereign's righteousness in treating gentlemen.

value.zh: 又鴻道王沖造作虛語，云足下量度吾心，不受沖說。
value.en: Li Hong also said Wang Chong’s story was invented, and he praised you for seeing my true intent and rejecting the lie.
value.literal: Again Hong related that Wang Chong fabricated empty words, saying you measured my mind and did not accept Chong's tale.

value.zh: 尋表明之言，追平生之好，依依東望，故遣有書。」
value.en: Clarifying what was declared above, pursuing the friendship of a lifetime, lingering as I gaze east—I therefore send this letter."
value.literal: Clarifying what was declared above, pursuing the friendship of a lifetime, lingering as I gaze east—I therefore send this letter."

value.zh: 達得亮書，數相交通，辭欲叛魏。
value.en: Meng Da answered repeatedly and began plotting to revolt from Wei.
value.literal: When Da obtained Liang's letter, repeatedly exchanged communication, declared intent wishing to rebel against Wei.

value.zh: 魏遣司馬宣王征之，即斬滅達。
value.en: Wei sent Sima Yi against him and had him killed at once.
value.literal: Wei sent Sima the King of Xuan to campaign against him; at once beheaded and destroyed Da.

value.zh: 亮亦以達無款誠之心，故不救助也。
value.en: Zhuge Liang did not send help because he judged Meng Da insincere.
value.literal: Liang also because Da had no sincere and honest heart, therefore did not rescue and aid.

value.zh: 蔣琬秉政，以詩為諫議大夫，卒於家。
value.en: Under Jiang Wan’s regency Fei Shi became grandee remonstrant and died at home.
value.literal: Jiang Wan held government, appointed Shi grandee remonstrant; he died at home.

value.zh: 黃權，字公衡，巴西閬中人也。
value.en: Huang Quan, styled Gongheng, came from Langzhong in Ba-Xi Commandery.
value.literal: Huang Quan, courtesy name Gongheng, was a man of Langzhong in Ba-Xi.

value.zh: 少為郡吏，州牧劉璋召為主簿。
value.en: He began as a county clerk until Yi Province Governor Liu Zhang named him chief clerk.
value.literal: In youth he was a county clerk; Governor Liu Zhang summoned him as chief clerk.

value.zh: 時別駕張鬆建議，宜迎先主，使伐張魯。
value.en: Zhang Song, Liu Zhang’s vice administrator, urged inviting Liu Bei west to attack Zhang Lu.
value.literal: At that time Vice Administrator Zhang Song proposed that it was fitting to welcome the First Sovereign and send him to campaign against Zhang Lu.

value.zh: 權諫曰：「左將軍有驍名，今請到，欲以部曲遇之，則不滿其心，欲以賓客禮待，則一國不容二君。
value.en: Huang Quan objected: “The Left General is famous as a fighter. Treat him like a subordinate and he will resent it; treat him as an honored guest and two masters cannot share one realm.
value.literal: Quan remonstrated, saying: 'The Left General has a fierce reputation; now if we invite him and wish to treat him as retainers [buqu], we will not satisfy his heart; if we wish to receive him with the rites due a guest, then one state cannot contain two lords.

value.zh: 若容有泰山之安，則主有累卵之危。
value.en: Your guest would stand firm as Taishan while you teeter like a stack of eggs.
value.literal: If the guest has the security of Mount Tai, then the lord has the peril of piled eggs.

value.zh: 可但閉境，以待河清。」
value.en: Better seal the passes and wait until the world settles.”
value.literal: One may simply close the borders and await the river running clear [i.e. peace in the realm].'

value.zh: 璋不聽，竟遣使迎先生，出權為廣漢長，及先主襲取益州，將帥分下郡縣。
value.en: Liu Zhang refused, sent an envoy to welcome Liu Bei anyway, and transferred Huang Quan out as chief of Guanghan. When Liu Bei seized Yi Province by surprise, generals and commanders spread through the commanderies and counties.
value.literal: Zhang did not listen; in the end he dispatched an envoy to welcome the First Sovereign; he transferred Quan out to be chief of Guanghan; when the First Sovereign seized Yi Province by surprise, generals and commanders fanned out into commanderies and counties.

value.zh: 郡縣風景附，權閉城堅守，須劉璋稽服，乃詣降先主。
value.en: County after county yielded; Huang Quan held his walls until Liu Zhang capitulated, then opened his gates to Liu Bei.
value.literal: Commanderies and counties submitted like wind and shadow [swiftly]; Quan closed the city and defended firmly; he waited until Liu Zhang bowed in submission, then went to surrender to the First Sovereign.

value.zh: 先主假權偏將軍。
value.en: Liu Bei named him acting lieutenant general.
value.literal: The First Sovereign appointed Quan acting Lieutenant General.

value.zh: 〈徐眾評曰：權既忠諫於主，又閉城拒守，得事君之禮。
value.en: 〈Xu Zhong remarks that Huang Quan both warned his lord faithfully and held his city—proper conduct for a minister.
value.literal: 〈Xu Zhong appraises: Quan both loyally remonstrated his lord and closed the city and resisted defense—he obtained the rites of serving a lord.

value.zh: 武王下車，封比干之墓，表商容之閭，所以大顯忠賢之士，而明示所貴之旨。
value.en: King Wu honored Bi Gan’s tomb and Shang Rong’s lane to proclaim loyalty—the standard Liu Bei should emulate.
value.literal: When King Wu stepped down from his chariot, he enfeoffed Bi Gan's tomb and marked Shang Rong's lane—thereby greatly displaying loyal and worthy men and clearly showing the aim of what is honored.

value.zh: 先主假權將軍，善矣，然猶薄少，未足彰忠義之高節，而大勸為善者之心。〉
value.en: Promoting him to general was decent but too modest to honor such steadfast loyalty or inspire others.〉
value.literal: That the First Sovereign appointed Quan general is good, yet still meager—it does not suffice to display the lofty integrity of loyalty and righteousness or greatly encourage the hearts of those who do good.〉

value.zh: 及曹公破張魯，魯走入巴中，權進曰：「若失漢中，則三巴不振，此為割蜀之股臂也。」
value.en: When Cao Cao drove Zhang Lu into Bazhong, Huang Quan urged: “Lose Hanzhong and the Three Ba collapse—you would sever Shu’s limbs.”
value.literal: When Duke Cao defeated Zhang Lu, Lu fled into Ba-Zhong; Quan advanced his view, saying: 'If we lose Hanzhong, then the Three Ba will not flourish—this is cutting off Shu's thigh and arm.'

value.zh: 於是先主以權為護軍，率諸將迎魯，魯已還南鄭，北降曹公。
value.en: Liu Bei made Huang Quan protector of the army and marched to intercept Zhang Lu, but Zhang Lu had already doubled back to Nan Zheng and surrendered to Cao Cao.
value.literal: Thereupon the First Sovereign appointed Quan Protector of the Army and led the various generals to welcome Lu; Lu had already returned to Nan Zheng and submitted north to Duke Cao.

value.zh: 然卒破杜濩、樸胡，殺夏候淵，據漢中，皆權本謀也。
value.en: Yet the victories over Du Hu and Pu Hu, the death of Xiahou Yuan, and the seizure of Hanzhong all stemmed from Huang Quan’s original plan.
value.literal: Yet in the end [they] defeated Du Hu and Pu Hu, killed Xiahou Yuan, and occupied Hanzhong—all were Quan's original stratagem.

value.zh: 後領益州刺史，徙佔河南。
value.en: He later held concurrent rank as Inspector of Yi Province and moved to reside south of the Yellow River.
value.literal: Later he concurrently served as Inspector of Yi Province and shifted to reside south of the Yellow River [in Wei territory].

value.zh: 大將軍司馬宣王深器之，問權曰：「蜀中有卿輩幾人？」
value.en: Grand General Sima Yi thought highly of him and asked, “How many men like you remain in Shu?”
value.literal: Grand General Sima Yi deeply esteemed him and asked Quan, saying: 'How many men like you, sir, are there in Shu?'

value.zh: 權笑而答曰：「不圖明公見顧之重也！」
value.en: Huang Quan smiled and said, “I hardly expected such attention from you.”
value.literal: Quan smiled and replied: 'I did not expect the illustrious lord to regard me so heavily!'

value.zh: 宣王與諸葛亮書曰：「黃公衡，快士也，每坐起歎述足下，不去口實。」
value.en: Sima Yi wrote Zhuge Liang: “Huang Gongheng is a blunt-spoken man who speaks of you whenever he rises or sits.”
value.literal: King Xuan wrote to Zhuge Liang, saying: 'Huang Gongheng is a forthright knight; each time he sits or rises he sighs and narrates you—words do not leave his mouth.'

value.zh: 景初三年，蜀延熙二年，權遷車騎將軍、儀同三司。
value.en: In 239 Wei’s third year of Jingchu and Shu’s second year of Yanxi he became general of chariots and cavalry with Three Excellencies protocol.
value.literal: In the third year of Jingchu [239], the second year of Yanxi in Shu [239], Quan was promoted General of Chariots and Cavalry with ceremonial parity of the Three Offices.

value.zh: 〈《蜀記》曰：魏明帝問權：「天下鼎立，當以何地為正？」
value.en: 〈The Shu ji records that Emperor Ming of Wei asked Huang Quan which place should be considered orthodox while the realm stood like a tripod.
value.literal: 〈The Shu Ji states: Emperor Ming of Wei asked Quan: 'The realm stands like a tripod—what place should be considered orthodox?'

value.zh: 權對曰：「當以天文為正。
value.en: Huang Quan answered: “Heaven’s omens decide legitimacy.
value.literal: Quan replied: 'One should take celestial signs as orthodox.

value.zh: 往者熒惑守心而文皇帝崩，吳、蜀二主平安，此其徵也。」〉
value.en: When Mars lodged in the Heart and Wei’s Emperor Wen died, the rulers of Wu and Shu were untouched—that is the proof.”〉
value.literal: Formerly Mars lodged in the Heart [constellation] and Emperor Wen died; the two lords of Wu and Shu were safe—this is its proof.'〉"

value.zh: 明年卒，謚曰景侯。
value.en: He died the following year with the posthumous title Marquis Jing.
value.literal: The next year he died; his posthumous title was Marquis Jing.

value.zh: 子邕嗣、邕無子，絕。
value.en: His son Huang Yong inherited but died without heirs, so the marquisate lapsed.
value.literal: His son Yong succeeded; Yong had no son—the line ended.

value.zh: 權留蜀子祟，為尚書郎，隨衛將軍諸葛瞻拒鄧艾。
value.en: Huang Quan’s son Huang Chong stayed in Shu as a masters-of-writing gentleman and followed Guardian General Zhuge Zhan against Deng Ai.
value.literal: Quan left behind in Shu his son Chong, who was Gentleman of the Masters of Writing; he followed Guardian General Zhuge Zhan to resist Deng Ai.

value.zh: 到涪縣，瞻盤桓未近，祟屢勸瞻宜速行據險，無令敵得入平地。
value.en: At Fu County, Zhuge Zhan hesitated; Huang Chong urged him repeatedly to seize the passes before Deng Ai reached the plain.
value.literal: When they reached Fu County, Zhan lingered and did not advance near; Chong repeatedly urged Zhan that he ought swiftly to march and seize defiles—do not allow the enemy to reach level ground.

value.zh: 瞻猶與未納，祟至於流涕。
value.en: Zhuge Zhan still delayed until Huang Chong wept with frustration.
value.literal: Zhan still dallied and did not accept; Chong reached the point of shedding tears.

value.zh: 會艾長驅而前，瞻卻戰綿竹，祟帥厲軍士，期於必死，臨陣見殺。
value.en: Deng Ai swept forward; Zhuge Zhan fell back to Mianzhu. Huang Chong rallied the troops for a fight to the death and died in the front rank.
value.literal: As it happened Ai drove straight forward; Zhan withdrew to fight at Mianzhu; Chong led and exhorted the soldiers, expecting certain death; facing battle he was killed.

value.zh: 王平字子均，巴西宕渠人也。
value.en: Wang Ping, styled Zijun, came from Dangqu in Ba-Xi.
value.literal: Wang Ping, courtesy name Zijun, was a man of Dangqu in Ba-Xi.
